title.zh: 卷45 韋閬 杜銓 裴駿 辛紹先 柳崇
title.en: Volume 45: Wei Lang, Du Quan, Pei Jun, Xin Shaoxian, Liu Chong
title.raw: 卷45 韋閬 杜銓 裴駿 辛紹先 柳崇 Volume 45: Wei Lang, Du Quan, Pei Jun, Xin Shaoxian, Liu Chong

sentences.zh: 韋閬 杜銓 裴駿 辛紹先 柳崇

translations.literal: Wei Lang; Du Quan; Pei Jun; Xin Shaoxian; Liu Chong
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lang; Du Quan; Pei Jun; Xin Shaoxian; Liu Chong

sentences.zh: 韋閬，字友觀，京兆杜陵人。

translations.literal: Wei Lang, courtesy name Youguan, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lang, whose courtesy name was Youguan, came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 世為三輔冠族。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been a leading clan of the Three Adjuncts.
translations.idiomatic: His family had for generations ranked among the foremost clans of the Three Adjuncts.

sentences.zh: 袓楷，晉建威將軍、長樂清河二郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kai was Jin General Who Establishes Might and concurrently governor of the two commanderies of Changle and Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kai served Jin as General Who Establishes Might and as governor of both Changle and Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 父逵，慕容垂吏部郎、大長秋卿。

translations.literal: His father Kui was Murong Chui's Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kui held office under Murong Chui as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 閬少有器望，值慕容氏政亂，避地於薊城。

translations.literal: Lang in youth had capacity and reputation; when the Murong regime fell into disorder, he took refuge at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lang showed promise early on; when the Murong house fell into turmoil, he took refuge at Ji.

sentences.zh: 世祖徵拜咸陽太守，轉武都太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu summoned and appointed him governor of Xianyang, then transferred him to governor of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu summoned him to office as governor of Xianyang and later transferred him to Wudu.

sentences.zh: 屬杏城鎮將郝溫及蓋吳反，關中擾亂，閬盡心撫納，所部獨全。

translations.literal: When the garrison commander of Xingcheng, Hao Wen, and Gai Wu rebelled and Guanzhong was thrown into turmoil, Lang devoted himself to comforting and winning people over, and his jurisdiction alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xingcheng garrison commander Hao Wen and Gai Wu rose in rebellion and Guanzhong was thrown into chaos, Lang devoted himself to comforting and winning people over, and his district alone remained secure.

sentences.zh: 在郡十六年，卒。

translations.literal: After sixteen years in the commandery, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the commandery for sixteen years and then died.

sentences.zh: 子範，歷鎮西大將軍府司馬，試守華山郡。

translations.literal: His son Fan successively served as staff officer in the Grand General Who Pacifies the West's headquarters and as acting administrator of Huashan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan served as staff officer on the staff of the Grand General Who Pacifies the West and as acting administrator of Huashan commandery.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，賜爵興平男。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wencheng's time he was granted the title Baron of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wencheng he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子儁，字穎超，早有學識。

translations.literal: His son Jun, courtesy name Yingchao, early possessed learning and insight.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun, courtesy name Yingchao, was learned from an early age.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事祖母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his grandmother and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he cared for his grandmother and won renown for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 性溫和廉讓，為州里所稱。

translations.literal: His nature was gentle, temperate, and modest; he was praised throughout the province and district.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle, temperate, and modest by nature, he was praised throughout his home district.

sentences.zh: 太和中，襲爵。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he inherited the family title.

sentences.zh: 除荊州治中，轉梁州寧朔府長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed aide to the governor of Jing province, then transferred to chief clerk of Liang province's Ningshuo headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed aide to the governor of Jing province, then transferred to chief clerk on the Ningshuo staff in Liang province.

sentences.zh: 還，為太尉外兵參軍、本州中正，遷都水使者。

translations.literal: On his return he became Outside Troops Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant and chief rectifier of his native province, then was promoted to Commissioner of the Capital Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he served as Outside Troops Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant and as chief rectifier of his home province, and was later promoted to Commissioner of the Capital Waterways.

sentences.zh: 所在有聲。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he gained a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，領軍于忠矯擅威刑，與左僕射郭祚、尚書裴植同時遇害，語在植傳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died, the Director of the Army Yu Zhong perverted authority and wielded punishments arbitrarily; together with Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Guo Zuo and Master of Writing Pei Zhi he was killed at the same time—the account is in Zhi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, the Director of the Army Yu Zhong abused his power and punished at will; Jun fell victim together with Left Vice Director Guo Zuo and Master of Writing Pei Zhi—the full account appears in Pei Zhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 時年五十七。

translations.literal: He was fifty-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-seven at the time.

sentences.zh: 儁與祚婚家，為忠所惡，故及於難。

translations.literal: Jun was related by marriage to Zuo and was hated by Zhong, and so he met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was connected by marriage to Guo Zuo and was detested by Yu Zhong, and so he was swept into the calamity.

sentences.zh: 臨終，儁訴枉於尚書元欽，欽知而不敢申理。

translations.literal: At the end Jun pleaded his innocence to Master of Writing Yuan Qin; Qin knew but did not dare to press the case.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Jun protested his innocence to Master of Writing Yuan Qin, who knew the truth yet did not dare to intervene.

sentences.zh: 儁歎曰：「吾一生為善，未蒙善報；

translations.literal: Jun sighed and said, "All my life I have done good, yet I have not received good in return;
translations.idiomatic: Jun sighed and said, "All my life I have done good, yet I have never been repaid with good;

sentences.zh: 常不為惡，今為惡終。

translations.literal: I have never done evil, yet now I end in evil.
translations.idiomatic: I have never done evil, yet now I meet an evil end.

sentences.zh: 悠悠蒼天，抱直無訴！」

translations.literal: Vast, vast azure Heaven—upright yet with no one to hear my plea!"
translations.idiomatic: O vast azure Heaven, I hold to what is right yet have no one to hear my plea!"

sentences.zh: 時人咸怨傷焉。

translations.literal: People of the time all grieved and resented on his account.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time all grieved and resented what had been done to him.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年，追贈中壘將軍、洛州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiping he was posthumously given the posts of General of the Central Ramparts and governor of Luo province, with the posthumous title Upright.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiping he was posthumously honored as General of the Central Ramparts and governor of Luo province, with the posthumous name Upright.

sentences.zh: 有子十三人。

translations.literal: He had thirteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left thirteen sons.

sentences.zh: 長子榮緒，字子光，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Rongxu, courtesy name Ziguan, was fairly versed in letters and history.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Rongxu, courtesy name Ziguan, was well versed in letters and history.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，除員外散騎侍郎、齊王蕭寶夤儀同開府屬，因戰敗歿。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and was appointed Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and staff member on Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin's Equaling-the-Three-Ministers headquarters, and died when the army was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and was appointed Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and a staff member on Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin's headquarters with the rank Equaling the Three Ministers; he perished when the army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 榮緒弟榮茂，字子曄。

translations.literal: Rongxu's younger brother Rongmao, courtesy name Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: Rongxu's younger brother Rongmao, whose courtesy name was Ziye.

sentences.zh: 以幹局知名。

translations.literal: He was known for practical ability and administrative grasp.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for practical ability and sound judgment in office.

sentences.zh: 歷侍御史、尚書考功郎中。

translations.literal: He successively served as attendant censor and Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Merit Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as attendant censor and as Director in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Merit Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 出為征虜將軍、東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and governor of Eastern Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and governor of Eastern Qin province.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，兄弟並歿關西。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongxi era both brothers died in Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongxi era both brothers perished in the west.

sentences.zh: 榮茂弟子粲，為寶炬南汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Rongmao's nephew Zican served as governor of Southern Fen province under Bao Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Rongmao's nephew Zican served Bao Ju as governor of Southern Fen province.

sentences.zh: 子粲少弟道諧，為南汾州鎮城都督。

translations.literal: Zican's younger brother Daoxie was garrison commander of the walled city in Southern Fen province.
translations.idiomatic: Zican's younger brother Daoxie was commander of the walled garrison in Southern Fen province.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王命將出討，陷城克之。

translations.literal: King Xianwu of Qi ordered a general to march out against them; the city was taken by assault.
translations.idiomatic: King Xianwu of Qi sent a general against them, stormed the city, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 武定末，子粲官至南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuding era Zican rose to governor of Southern Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Wuding era Zican had risen to governor of Southern Yan province.

sentences.zh: 閬兄子真喜，起家中書博士，遷中書侍郎、馮翊太守。

translations.literal: Lang's elder brother's son Zhenxi entered office as Doctor of the Secretariat and was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and governor of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's nephew Zhenxi entered office as Doctor of the Secretariat and was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and governor of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 子祉，卒於太府少卿。

translations.literal: His son Zhi died while serving as Vice Director of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi died in office as Vice Director of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 祉子義遠，出帝時，為岐州刺史，沒關西。

translations.literal: Zhi's son Yiyuan, in Emperor Chu's time, was governor of Qi province and was lost in Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son Yiyuan served under Emperor Chu as governor of Qi province and was lost in the west.

sentences.zh: 祉弟禎，有識幹。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Zhen had insight and practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Zhen was a man of insight and practical ability.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: He began his career as a court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a court attendant.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎中、司徒主簿、太子中舍人、廷尉少卿、給事黃門侍郎、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He served as Director in the Masters of Writing, chief clerk to the Minister of Education, Palace Attendant in the Household of the Heir Apparent, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gates with the duty of presenting memorials, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Director in the Masters of Writing, chief clerk to the Minister of Education, Palace Attendant in the Heir Apparent's household, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安西將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the posts of General Who Pacifies the West and governor of Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the West and governor of Qin province.

sentences.zh: 子文殊，員外散騎侍郎，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Wenshu was Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenshu served as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and died young.

sentences.zh: 閬從叔道福。

translations.literal: Lang's paternal uncle Daofu.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's paternal uncle Daofu.

sentences.zh: 父羆，為苻堅丞相王猛所器重，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: His father Pi was highly regarded by Fu Jian's Chancellor Wang Meng, who gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pi won the esteem of Fu Jian's chancellor Wang Meng, who gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 為堅東海太守。

translations.literal: He served Fu Jian as governor of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He served Fu Jian as governor of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 堅滅，奔江左，仕劉裕為輔國將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian was destroyed, he fled to the lands south of the Yangzi and served Liu Yu as General Who Assists the State and governor of Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian's state fell, he fled south of the Yangzi and served Liu Yu as General Who Assists the State and governor of Qin province.

sentences.zh: 道福有志略，歷劉駿盱眙、南沛二郡太守，領鎮北府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Daofu had ambition and strategy; he successively governed the two commanderies of Xuyi and Nanpei under Liu Jun and served as recording secretary in the Pacify-the-North headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu was a man of ambition and strategy; he served Liu Jun as governor of Xuyi and Nanpei in turn and as recording secretary on the Pacify-the-North staff.

sentences.zh: 時徐州刺史薛安都謀欲擁州內附，道福參贊其事。

translations.literal: At that time the governor of Xu province, Xue Andu, plotted to bring the province over to allegiance with the north, and Daofu assisted and advised in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When the governor of Xu province, Xue Andu, plotted to surrender the province to the north, Daofu took part in planning the move.

sentences.zh: 以功除安遠將軍，賜爵高密侯，因此仍家於彭城。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and granted the title Marquis of Gaomi, and on that account his family thereafter settled at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaomi; his family thereafter made their home at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、兗州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the posts of General Who Punishes the Barbarians and governor of Yan province, with the posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and governor of Yan province, with the posthumous name Simple.

sentences.zh: 子欣宗，以歸國勳，別賜爵杜縣侯。

translations.literal: His son Xinzong, for merit in returning to allegiance, was separately granted the title Marquis of Du county.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xinzong, for merit in returning to the north, was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Du county.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，拜彭城內史，遷大將軍、宋王劉昶諮議參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was appointed internal administrator of Pengcheng and was transferred to advisory staff officer on the staff of the Grand General, Prince of Song Liu Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign he was appointed internal administrator of Pengcheng, then transferred to advisory staff officer on Grand General Liu Chang, Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 廣陵侯元衍為徐州刺史，又請為長史，帶彭城內史。

translations.literal: When Marquis of Guangling Yuan Yan became governor of Xu province, he again requested Xinzong as chief clerk, concurrently holding the post of internal administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis of Guangling Yuan Yan became governor of Xu province, he again asked for Xinzong as his chief clerk, with concurrent duty as internal administrator of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 撫綏內外，甚得民和。

translations.literal: He comforted and settled those within and without, and greatly won the people's accord.
translations.idiomatic: He won people over within and without the administration, and the district grew notably harmonious.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，除通直散騎常侍，出為河北太守，不行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was appointed Regular Palace Attendant and sent out as governor of Hebei, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was appointed Regular Palace Attendant and offered the governorship of Hebei, but he declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太中大夫、行幽州事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand Master of Palace Counsel and acted for the affairs of You province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Grand Master of Palace Counsel and placed in charge of You province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈龍驤將軍、南兗州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the posts of Dragon-Coursing General and governor of Southern Yan province, with the posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Dragon-Coursing General and governor of Southern Yan province, with the posthumous name Simple.

sentences.zh: 子元叡，武定中，潁州驃騎府長史。

translations.literal: His son Yuanrui, in the Wuding era, was chief clerk on the Rapid Cavalry headquarters of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanrui served in the Wuding era as chief clerk on the Rapid Cavalry staff in Ying province.

sentences.zh: 欣宗從父弟合宗，卒於東海太守。

translations.literal: Xinzong's paternal cousin Hezong died while serving as governor of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzong's paternal cousin Hezong died in office as governor of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 子元恢，有氣幹。

translations.literal: His son Yuanhui had spirit and practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanhui was a man of spirit and practical ability.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，值刺史元法僧據州外叛，元恢招聚同志，潛規克復，事泄，為法僧所害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xiaochang era, when the governor Yuan Faseng held the province and rebelled to the south, Yuanhui gathered like-minded men and secretly plotted recovery; the affair leaked out and he was killed by Faseng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaochang era, when Governor Yuan Faseng seized the province and defected, Yuanhui gathered allies and secretly plotted to recover it; when the plot was discovered, Faseng had him killed.

sentences.zh: 時人傷惜之。

translations.literal: People of the time grieved and lamented for him.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 閬從子崇，字洪基。

translations.literal: Lang's nephew Chong, courtesy name Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's nephew Chong, whose courtesy name was Hongji.

sentences.zh: 父肅，字道壽。

translations.literal: His father Su, courtesy name Daoshou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Su, whose courtesy name was Daoshou.

sentences.zh: 劉義真鎮關中，辟為主簿，仍隨義真度江，歷魏郡弋陽二郡太守、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Liu Yizhen garrisoned Guanzhong he recruited Su as chief clerk; Su then followed Yizhen in crossing the Yangzi and successively governed the two commanderies of Wei and Yiyang and served as governor of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yizhen held Guanzhong he recruited Su as chief clerk; Su followed him across the Yangzi and later served in turn as governor of Wei and Yiyang and as governor of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 崇年十歲，父卒，母鄭氏以入國，因寓居河洛。

translations.literal: Chong was ten when his father died; his mother, Lady Zheng, entered the north with the court and so they took up residence in the He and Luo region.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was ten when his father died; his mother Lady Zheng came north with the court, and the family settled in the He-Luo region.

sentences.zh: 少為舅兗州刺史鄭羲所器賞。

translations.literal: In youth he was esteemed and favored by his maternal uncle Zheng Xi, governor of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he won the esteem of his maternal uncle Zheng Xi, governor of Yan province.

sentences.zh: [1]解褐中書博士，轉司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: [1] Leaving the russet robe, he became Doctor of the Secretariat and was transferred to Attendant in the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: [1] On entering office he was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat and later transferred to Attendant in the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 高祖納其女為充華嬪。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu took his daughter as a Filling-the-Harem concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu took his daughter into the palace as a Filling-the-Harem concubine.

sentences.zh: 除南潁川太守，不好發摘細事，常云：「何用小察，以傷大道。」

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Southern Yingchuan; he did not like to expose and pursue petty matters, and often said, "Why use petty scrutiny and harm the great Way?"
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Southern Yingchuan; he disliked hunting out petty offenses and often said, "Why trouble with petty scrutiny and wound the greater principle?"

sentences.zh: 吏民感之，郡中大治。

translations.literal: Officials and people were moved by this, and the commandery was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners were moved by this, and the commandery was brought to excellent order.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘉賞，賜帛二百匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu heard of it and commended him, bestowing two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu heard of it he praised him and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，以崇為司州中正，尋除右將軍，咸陽王禧開府從事中郎，復為河南邑中正。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, Chong was made chief rectifier of Si province; soon he was appointed General of the Right and Attendant on Prince of Xianyang Xi's headquarters, and again served as chief rectifier of Henan district.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved to Luoyang, Chong was made chief rectifier of Si province; he was soon appointed General of the Right and Attendant on Prince of Xianyang Xi's staff, and again served as chief rectifier of Henan district.

sentences.zh: 崇頻居衡品，以平直見稱。

translations.literal: Chong repeatedly held the office of rating ranks and was praised for fairness and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Chong repeatedly held office as rank-rater and was praised for fairness and integrity.

sentences.zh: 出為鄉郡太守，更滿應代，吏民詣闕乞留，復延三年。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Xiang commandery; when his term was full and he was due to be replaced, officials and people went to the court to beg that he be kept, and his tenure was extended for three more years.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Xiang commandery; when his term ended and he was due to be replaced, officials and commoners petitioned at court to keep him, and his tenure was extended for three years.

sentences.zh: 在郡九年，轉司徒諮議。

translations.literal: After nine years in the commandery he was transferred to advisory staff officer to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years in the commandery he was transferred to advisory staff officer to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 久之，除華山太守，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed governor of Huashan and died.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he was appointed governor of Huashan and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子猷之，釋褐奉朝請，轉給事中、步兵校尉，稍遷前將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: His son Youzhi, on leaving the russet robe, became a court attendant, then was transferred to Palace Attendant and Colonel of Footsoldiers, and gradually rose to General of the Vanguard and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youzhi entered office as a court attendant, then served as Palace Attendant and Colonel of Footsoldiers, and gradually rose to General of the Vanguard and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 猷之弟休之，起家安州左將軍府城局參軍，轉給事中、河南邑中正，稍遷安西將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Youzhi's younger brother Xiuzhi began his career as staff officer in the walled-city bureau of the Left General's headquarters in An province, was transferred to Palace Attendant and chief rectifier of Henan district, and gradually rose to General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's younger brother Xiuzhi began as a staff officer in the walled-city bureau on the Left General's staff in An province, then served as Palace Attendant and chief rectifier of Henan district, and gradually rose to General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 休之貞和自守，未嘗以言行忤物。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi was upright and harmonious in self-restraint and never gave offense in word or deed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi was upright and even-tempered and never gave offense in word or deed.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子道建，武定末，定州儀同開府長史，帶中山太守。

translations.literal: His son Daojian, at the end of the Wuding era, was chief clerk on the Equaling-the-Three-Ministers headquarters of Ding province, concurrently holding the post of governor of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daojian, late in the Wuding era, was chief clerk on the Equaling-the-Three-Ministers staff in Ding province, with concurrent duty as governor of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 道建弟道儒，齊文襄王大將軍府東閤祭酒。

translations.literal: Daojian's younger brother Daoru was libationer of the Eastern Pavilion on King Wenxiang of Qi's Grand General headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Daojian's younger brother Daoru served as libationer of the Eastern Pavilion on King Wenxiang of Qi's Grand General staff.

sentences.zh: 閬族弟珍，字靈智，高祖賜名焉。

translations.literal: Lang's clansman Zhen, courtesy name Lingzhi, was given his name by Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's kinsman Zhen, courtesy name Lingzhi, received his given name from Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 父尚，字文叔，樂安王良安西府從事中郎。

translations.literal: His father Shang, courtesy name Wenshu, was Attendant in Prince of Le'an Liang's Pacify-the-West headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shang, courtesy name Wenshu, served as Attendant on Prince of Le'an Liang's Pacify-the-West staff.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安遠將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the posts of General Who Pacifies the Distance and governor of Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the Distance and governor of Yong province.

sentences.zh: 珍少有志操。

translations.literal: Zhen in youth had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen showed strong character from youth.

sentences.zh: 解褐京兆王子推常侍，轉尚書南部郎。

translations.literal: Leaving the russet robe, he became Regular Attendant to the Prince of Jingzhao, Zituo, and was transferred to Director in the Masters of Writing, Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he became Regular Attendant to Prince of Jingzhao Zituo and was later transferred to Director in the Masters of Writing, Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，蠻首桓誕歸款，朝廷思安邊之略，以誕為東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign the barbarian leader Huan Dan submitted in allegiance; the court considered strategies to settle the frontier and appointed Dan governor of Eastern Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign the barbarian leader Huan Dan came over in submission; the court sought a policy to secure the frontier and appointed Dan governor of Eastern Jing province.

sentences.zh: 令珍為使，與誕招慰蠻左。

translations.literal: Zhen was ordered to serve as envoy and, together with Dan, to summon and comfort the barbarians of the left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was sent as envoy to work with Dan in winning over the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 珍自懸瓠西入三百餘里，至桐栢山，窮淮源，宣揚恩澤，莫不降附。

translations.literal: Zhen from Xuanhuo marched west more than three hundred li to Mount Tongbai, traced the Huai to its source, proclaimed imperial favor, and none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen marched west from Xuanhuo more than three hundred li to Mount Tongbai, traced the Huai to its source, proclaimed the court's grace, and won the submission of all he met.

sentences.zh: 淮源舊有祠堂，蠻俗恒用人祭之。

translations.literal: At the Huai's source there was an old shrine; barbarian custom constantly used human victims in its rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the Huai's source stood an old shrine where, by tribal custom, human victims were regularly offered.

sentences.zh: 珍乃曉告曰：「天地明靈，即是民之父母，豈有父母甘子肉味！

translations.literal: Zhen then instructed them, saying, "The luminous spirits of Heaven and Earth are the people's parents—how could parents relish the taste of their children's flesh!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then explained to them, "The luminous spirits of Heaven and Earth are the people's parents—how could parents relish the flesh of their own children!

sentences.zh: 自今已後，悉宜以酒脯代用。」

translations.literal: From this time forward, wine and dried meat should all be used instead."
translations.idiomatic: From now on you should offer wine and dried meat instead."

sentences.zh: 羣蠻從約，至今行之。

translations.literal: The mass of barbarians accepted the covenant, and the practice continues to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes accepted the agreement, and the practice continues to this day.

sentences.zh: 凡所招降七萬餘戶，置郡縣而還。

translations.literal: In all he won the submission of more than seventy thousand households, established commanderies and counties, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In all he brought over more than seventy thousand households, set up commanderies and counties, and returned.

sentences.zh: 以奉使稱旨，除左將軍、樂陵鎮將，賜爵霸城子。

translations.literal: Because his mission answered to the imperial intent, he was appointed General of the Left and garrison commander of Leling, and granted the title Viscount of Bacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mission pleased the throne, he was appointed General of the Left and garrison commander of Leling and enfeoffed as Viscount of Bacheng.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成司州民謝天蓋自署司州刺史，規欲以州內附。

translations.literal: Xie Tiangai, a commoner of Si province under Xiao Daocheng, styled himself governor of Si province and plotted to bring the province over in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiangai, a subject of Si province under Xiao Daocheng, declared himself governor and plotted to surrender the province to the north.

sentences.zh: 事泄，為道成將崔慧景攻圍。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out and he was besieged by Daocheng's general Cui Huijing.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, he was besieged by Daocheng's general Cui Huijing.

sentences.zh: 詔珍率在鎮士馬渡淮援接。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhen to lead the garrison troops and horses across the Huai to relieve and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zhen to lead the garrison troops across the Huai to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 時道成聞珍將至，遣將苟元賓據淮逆拒。

translations.literal: At that time Daocheng, hearing that Zhen was coming, sent the general Gou Yuanbin to hold the Huai and resist.
translations.idiomatic: When Daocheng learned that Zhen was approaching, he sent General Gou Yuanbin to hold the Huai and block him.

sentences.zh: 珍乃分遣鐵馬，於上流潛渡，親率步士與賊對接。

translations.literal: Zhen then detached iron cavalry to cross secretly upstream and personally led foot soldiers to engage the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen sent iron cavalry to ford secretly upstream while he personally led infantry to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 旗鼓始交，甲騎奄至，腹背奮擊，破之。

translations.literal: As banners and drums first clashed, armored horsemen suddenly arrived and struck front and rear with full force, breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies first clashed, armored horsemen suddenly appeared and struck from front and rear, routing the enemy.

sentences.zh: 天蓋尋為左右所殺，降於慧景。

translations.literal: Before long Tiangai was killed by those around him and surrendered to Huijing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tiangai was killed by his own followers and the remnant surrendered to Huijing.

sentences.zh: 珍乘勝馳進，又破慧景，擁降民七千餘戶內徙，表置城陽、剛陵、義陽三郡以處之。

translations.literal: Zhen pressed the victory in rapid pursuit, again defeated Huijing, and moved more than seven thousand surrendered households inland, memorializing to establish the three commanderies of Chengyang, Gangling, and Yiyang to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen pressed the pursuit, defeated Huijing again, resettled more than seven thousand surrendered households inland, and memorialized for the establishment of Chengyang, Gangling, and Yiyang commanderies to receive them.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔珍移鎮比陽，[2]蕭賾遣其雍州刺史陳顯達率眾來寇。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered Zhen to transfer his garrison to Biyang; Xiao Ze sent his governor of Yong province, Chen Xianda, leading troops to invade.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ordered Zhen to move his garrison to Biyang; Xiao Ze sent Chen Xianda, governor of Yong province, at the head of an army to attack.

sentences.zh: 城中將士咸欲出戰，珍曰：「彼初至氣銳，未可便挫，且共堅守，待其攻我疲弊，擊之未晚。」

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers in the city all wished to go out and fight; Zhen said, "They have just arrived and their spirit is keen—we must not blunt it rashly. Let us hold the walls together and wait until they grow weary attacking us; then it will not be too late to strike."
translations.idiomatic: The garrison wanted to sally forth, but Zhen said, "They have just arrived and their spirit is high—we should not engage them rashly. Let us hold the walls until they tire of the assault; then we can strike."

sentences.zh: 於是憑城拒戰，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon relying on the walls they resisted; casualties were very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: They held the walls and fought; casualties on both sides were heavy.

sentences.zh: 相持旬有二日，夜開城門掩擊之，賊遂奔潰。

translations.literal: After holding out for twelve days, at night they opened the gates and made a surprise attack; the enemy then fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: After twelve days of stalemate they opened the gates by night and struck; the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為侯。

translations.literal: For his merit his title was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For his service his rank was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 車駕南討，珍上便宜，并自陳在邊歲久，悉其要害，願為前驅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Zhen submitted timely proposals and himself stated that after many years on the frontier he knew all the vital points and wished to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Zhen submitted practical proposals and declared that after long service on the frontier he knew every strategic point and asked to serve as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 詔珍為隴西公源懷衞大將軍府長史，轉太保、齊郡王長史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhen chief clerk on Duke of Longxi Yuan Huai's Guard-the-General headquarters, then transferred him to chief clerk to the Grand Mentor and Prince of Qi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk on Duke of Longxi Yuan Huai's staff, then transferred to chief clerk to the Grand Mentor, Prince of Qi commandery.

sentences.zh: 遷顯武將軍、郢州刺史，在州有聲績，朝庭嘉之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of Manifest Martial Power and governor of Ying province; in the province he had reputation and achievement, and the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Manifest Martial Power and governor of Ying province, where he earned a strong record that the court commended.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍，賜驊騮二匹、帛五十匹、穀三百斛。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Dragon-Coursing General and was given two chestnut horses, fifty bolts of silk, and three hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Dragon-Coursing General and received two chestnut horses, fifty bolts of silk, and three hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 珍乃召集州內孤貧者，謂曰：「天子以我能綏撫卿等，故賜以穀帛，吾何敢獨當。」

translations.literal: Zhen then summoned the orphaned and poor within the province and said to them, "The Son of Heaven granted grain and silk because he believes I can comfort you—how could I keep it for myself alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen gathered the orphaned and destitute of the province and said, "The Son of Heaven gave me grain and silk because he believes I can care for you—how could I keep it for myself?"

sentences.zh: 遂以所賜悉分與之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he distributed everything he had been given.
translations.idiomatic: He then distributed the entire gift among them.

sentences.zh: 尋加平南將軍、荊州刺史，與尚書盧淵征赭陽，為蕭鸞將垣歷生、蔡道貴所敗，免歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional post of General Who Pacifies the South and governor of Jing province; together with Master of Writing Lu Yuan he campaigned against Zheyang and was defeated by Xiao Luan's generals Yuan Lisheng and Cai Daogui, then dismissed and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General Who Pacifies the South and governor of Jing province; campaigning against Zheyang with Master of Writing Lu Yuan, he was defeated by Xiao Luan's generals Yuan Lisheng and Cai Daogui and returned home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 臨別謂淵曰：「主上聖明，志吞吳會，用兵機要，在於上流。

translations.literal: On parting he told Yuan, "Our lord is sage and wise and aims to swallow Wu and Yue; the crucial point in using arms lies in the upper Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: On parting he told Yuan, "Our lord is wise and aims to conquer the southeast; the decisive theater of war lies on the upper Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 若有事荊楚，恐老夫復不得停耳。」

translations.literal: If there is trouble in Jing and Chu, I fear this old man will not be allowed to rest again."
translations.idiomatic: If trouble breaks out in Jing and Chu, I fear this old man will be called back again."

sentences.zh: 後車駕征樊郢，復起珍為中軍大將軍、彭城王勰長史。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage campaigned against Fan and Ying, Zhen was again raised to Grand General of the Central Army and chief clerk to Prince of Pengcheng Xie.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later campaigned against Fan and Ying, Zhen was recalled as Grand General of the Central Army and chief clerk to Prince of Pengcheng Xie.

sentences.zh: 沔北既平，以珍為建威將軍，試守魯陽郡。

translations.literal: Once the north bank of the Mian was pacified, Zhen was made General Who Establishes Might and acting administrator of Luyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the north bank of the Mian was pacified, Zhen was appointed General Who Establishes Might and acting administrator of Luyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖復南伐，路經珍郡，加中壘將軍，正太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu campaigned south again, his route passed through Zhen's commandery; Zhen was given the additional post of General of the Central Ramparts and confirmed as governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu marched south again, his route passed through Zhen's commandery; Zhen was promoted to General of the Central Ramparts and confirmed as full governor.

sentences.zh: 珍從至濟水，[3]高祖曰：「朕頃戎車再駕，卿常翼務中軍，今日之舉，亦欲與卿同行。

translations.literal: Zhen followed as far as the Ji River; Emperor Gaozu said, "I have lately twice taken the field, and you have constantly assisted in the central army's affairs; in today's campaign I also wished to go with you.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen accompanied him as far as the Ji River; Emperor Gaozu said, "I have lately taken the field twice, and you have always served at the center of the army; on this campaign too I wished to have you with me.

sentences.zh: 但三鵶險惡，非卿無以守也。」

translations.literal: But Sanyu is rugged and dangerous—without you it cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: But Sanyu is rugged and dangerous—only you can hold it."

sentences.zh: 因敕珍辭還。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered Zhen to take leave and return.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered Zhen to turn back.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩於行宮，祕匿而還，至珍郡始發大諱。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu died at the traveling palace the death was kept secret until the return; only when they reached Zhen's commandery was the great mourning proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu died at the traveling palace the death was kept secret on the return journey; the great mourning was proclaimed only when they reached Zhen's commandery.

sentences.zh: 還，除中散大夫，尋加鎮遠將軍、太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Palace Counsel; soon he was given the additional posts of General Who Pacifies the Distance and advisory staff officer to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed Palace Counsel and soon made General Who Pacifies the Distance and advisory staff officer to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 永平元年卒，時年七十四。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongping he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Yongping, at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、南青州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given his former generalship and the governorship of Southern Qing province, with the posthumous title Majestic.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with his former rank and the governorship of Southern Qing province, with the posthumous name Majestic.

sentences.zh: 長子纘，字遵彥。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zuan, courtesy name Zunyan.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zuan, whose courtesy name was Zunyan.

sentences.zh: 年十三，補中書學生，聰敏明辯，為博士李彪所稱。

translations.literal: At thirteen he was appointed a student of the Secretariat, clever, keen, and eloquent, praised by the erudite Li Biao.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he entered the Secretariat school; clever and articulate, he won praise from the erudite Li Biao.

sentences.zh: 除祕書中散，遷侍御中散。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Secretary Attendant and was transferred to Attendant in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Palace Secretary Attendant and later transferred to Attendant in the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖每與名德沙門談論往復，纘掌綴錄，無所遺漏，頗見知賞。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Gaozu debated back and forth with eminent Buddhist monks, Zuan took charge of compiling the record without omission and was much appreciated.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Gaozu debated with eminent Buddhist monks, Zuan recorded the exchanges without omission and won considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎侍郎，徙太子中舍人，仍兼黃門，又兼司徒右長史，尋轉長兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Cavalier, moved to Palace Attendant in the Heir Apparent's household while concurrently holding the Yellow Gates, then concurrently Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, and soon became chief clerk while also holding Left Director in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant Cavalier, then Palace Attendant in the Heir Apparent's household with concurrent duty at the Yellow Gates, then Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, and soon chief clerk with concurrent duty as Left Director in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 壽春內附，尚書令王肅出鎮揚州，請纘為長史，加平遠將軍，帶梁郡太守。

translations.literal: When Shouchun submitted, Master of Writing Wang Su went out to garrison Yang province and requested Zuan as chief clerk, with the additional post of General of Pacifying the Distance and concurrent governor of Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouchun came over, Master of Writing Wang Su went to garrison Yang province and asked for Zuan as chief clerk, with the additional rank of General of Pacifying the Distance and concurrent governorship of Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 肅薨，敕纘行州事。

translations.literal: When Su died, an edict ordered Zuan to act for the province's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Su died, an edict placed Zuan in charge of provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 任城王澄代肅為州，復啟纘為長史。

translations.literal: Prince of Rencheng Cheng replaced Su in the province and again requested Zuan as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Rencheng Cheng replaced Su as governor and again requested Zuan as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 澄出征之後，蕭衍將姜慶真乘虛攻襲，遂據外郭，雖尋克復，纘坐免官。

translations.literal: After Cheng marched out, Xiao Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen seized the moment to attack and took the outer wall; though it was soon recovered, Zuan was dismissed from office for the fault.
translations.idiomatic: After Cheng took the field, Xiao Yan's general Jiang Qingzhen attacked by surprise and seized the outer city; though it was soon recovered, Zuan was dismissed for the lapse.

sentences.zh: 永平三年卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongping he died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Yongping, at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 子彪，襲。

translations.literal: His son Biao inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Biao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 歷本州治中、轉別駕。

translations.literal: He successively served as aide to the governor of his native province and was transferred to vice administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide to the governor of his home province and was later transferred to vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 孝莊末，藍田太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiaozhuang era he was governor of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xiaozhuang era he was governor of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 沒於關西。

translations.literal: He was lost in Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was lost in the west.

sentences.zh: 彪弟融，解褐員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Biao's younger brother Rong, on leaving the russet robe, became Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's younger brother Rong entered office as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 以軍功賜爵長安伯。

translations.literal: For military merit he was granted the title Earl of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was enfeoffed as Earl of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 稍遷大司馬開府司馬。

translations.literal: He gradually rose to staff officer on the Grand Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually rose to staff officer on the Grand Marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 融娶司農卿趙郡李瑾女，天平中，疑其妻與章武王景哲姦通，乃刺殺之。

translations.literal: Rong married the daughter of Minister of Agriculture Li Jin of Zhao commandery; in the Tianping era, suspecting his wife of adultery with Prince of Zhangwu Yuan Jingzhe, he stabbed her to death.
translations.idiomatic: Rong married the daughter of Minister of Agriculture Li Jin of Zhao commandery; in the Tianping era, suspecting his wife of adultery with Prince of Zhangwu Yuan Jingzhe, he stabbed her to death.

sentences.zh: 懼不免，仍亦自害。

translations.literal: Fearing he could not escape punishment, he then killed himself as well.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he could not escape punishment, he then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 彧弟朏，字遵顯，少有志業。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Fei, courtesy name Zunxian, in youth had ambition and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger brother Fei, whose courtesy name was Zunxian, showed ambition and ability from youth.

sentences.zh: 年十八，辟州主簿。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was recruited as chief clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was recruited as the provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時屬歲儉，朏以家粟造粥，以飼飢人，所活甚眾。

translations.literal: As the year was lean, Fei used the family grain to make porridge to feed the hungry; very many were kept alive.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he used the family grain to make porridge for the hungry and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 解褐太學博士，遷祕書郎中，稍遷左軍將軍，為荊郢和糴大使。

translations.literal: Leaving the russet robe he became Erudite of the Imperial Academy, was transferred to Secretariat Director, and gradually rose to General of the Left Army and commissioner for harmonized grain purchase in Jing and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he became Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then Secretariat Director, and gradually rose to General of the Left Army and commissioner for harmonized grain purchase in Jing and Ying.

sentences.zh: 南郢州刺史田夷啟稱朏父珍往任荊州，恩洽夷夏，乞朏充南道別將，領荊州驍勇，共為腹背。

translations.literal: The governor of Southern Ying province, Tian Yi, memorialized that Fei's father Zhen had formerly served in Jing province and his kindness had reached both barbarians and Chinese, and begged that Fei be made separate commander of the southern route, leading Jing province's elite troops as mutual support front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Southern Ying Tian Yi memorialized that Fei's father Zhen had once governed Jing province with kindness that reached both tribes and Chinese, and asked that Fei serve as separate commander on the southern route with Jing's elite troops as mutual support.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，行南荊州事。

translations.literal: Before long he acted for the affairs of Southern Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: He soon acted for the affairs of Southern Jing province.

sentences.zh: 肅宗末，除征虜將軍、東徐州刺史，尋遷安東將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Suzong era he was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and governor of Eastern Xu province, then transferred to General Who Pacifies the East with the additional post of Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Suzong era he was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and governor of Eastern Xu province, then transferred to General Who Pacifies the East with the additional rank of Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣其郢州刺史田麤憘率眾來寇，朏於石羊崗破斬之，以功封杜縣開國子，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent his governor of Ying province, Tian Muchi, leading troops to invade; Fei at Shiyang Ridge defeated and beheaded him, and for his merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Du county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent Governor of Ying Tian Muchi against him; Fei defeated and killed him at Shiyang Ridge and was enfeoffed as Baron of Du county with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，卒於州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongan he died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the province in the third year of Yongan.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、車騎將軍、雍州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the posts of Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and governor of Yong province, with the posthumous title Proclaiming.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and governor of Yong province, with the posthumous name Proclaiming.

sentences.zh: 長子鴻，字道衍，頗有幹用。

translations.literal: His eldest son Hong, courtesy name Daoyan, had considerable practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Hong, whose courtesy name was Daoyan, was a capable man.

sentences.zh: 解褐奉朝請，遷尚書令吏部郎中、[4]中書舍人。

translations.literal: Leaving the russet robe he became a court attendant, was transferred to Director in the Masters of Writing's Bureau of Personnel and Palace Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as a court attendant, then served as Director in the Bureau of Personnel and as Palace Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天平三年，坐漏泄，賜死於家，時年三十二。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping, for leaking secrets he was ordered to die at home, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianping he was sentenced to death at home for leaking secrets, aged thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 鴻弟道植，武定末，儀同開府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Daozhi, at the end of the Wuding era, was Middle Troops Staff Officer on an Equaling-the-Three-Ministers headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's younger brother Daozhi, late in the Wuding era, was Middle Troops Staff Officer on an Equaling-the-Three-Ministers staff.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，有安定梁穎，先仕慕容寶，歷黃門郎。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizu's time there was Liang Ying of Anding, who had first served Murong Bao as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizu there was Liang Ying of Anding, who had earlier served Murong Bao as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 入國，拜建德太守，賜爵朝那男。

translations.literal: Entering the north he was appointed governor of Jiande and granted the title Baron of Chaona.
translations.idiomatic: After coming north he was appointed governor of Jiande and enfeoffed as Baron of Chaona.

sentences.zh: 孫景儁，起家趙郡王幹行參軍。

translations.literal: His grandson Jingjun began his career as mobile staff officer to Prince of Zhao commandery Gan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Jingjun began as mobile staff officer to Prince of Zhao commandery Gan.

sentences.zh: 稍遷治書侍御史、司徒中兵參軍。

translations.literal: He gradually rose to attendant censor for drafting imperial documents and Middle Troops Staff Officer to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant censor for drafting documents and Middle Troops Staff Officer to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子師禮，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Shili died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shili died young.

sentences.zh: 師禮族弟嵩遵，少有氣俠。

translations.literal: Shili's clansman Songzun in youth had spirit and chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Shili's kinsman Songzun in youth had spirit and chivalry.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請，歷司空外兵參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as a court attendant and successively served as Outside Troops Staff Officer to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a court attendant and served as Outside Troops Staff Officer to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 後蕭寶夤為雍州刺史，引為中兵參軍，深見信任。

translations.literal: Later, when Xiao Baoyin was governor of Yong province, he recruited him as Middle Troops Staff Officer and deeply trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xiao Baoyin governed Yong province, he recruited Songzun as Middle Troops Staff Officer and trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 寶夤反，令嵩遵率眾出征。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled he ordered Songzun to lead troops on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled he ordered Songzun to lead troops into the field.

sentences.zh: 嵩遵偽受其署，既行之後，遂與侯終德等還來襲城。

translations.literal: Songzun falsely accepted the commission; after setting out, he joined Hou Zhongde and others in turning back to assault the city.
translations.idiomatic: Songzun pretended to accept the commission, but after marching out he joined Hou Zhongde and others in turning back to storm the city.

sentences.zh: 以功封烏氏縣開國伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wushi county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wushi county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後除光州平東府長史，轉荊州驃騎府司馬。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed chief clerk on the Pacify-the-East headquarters of Guang province and transferred to staff officer on the Rapid Cavalry headquarters of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later chief clerk on the Pacify-the-East staff in Guang province and then staff officer on the Rapid Cavalry staff in Jing province.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年四十四。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 嵩遵弟嵩景，武定中，燕郡太守。

translations.literal: Songzun's younger brother Songjing, in the Wuding era, was governor of Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Songzun's younger brother Songjing served in the Wuding era as governor of Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 又有武功蘇湛，字景儁，魏侍中則之後也。

translations.literal: There was also Su Zhan of Wugong, courtesy name Jingjun, a descendant of Wei Attendant-in-Ordinary Ze.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Su Zhan of Wugong, courtesy name Jingjun, a descendant of Wei Attendant-in-Ordinary Ze.

sentences.zh: 晉亂，避地河右。

translations.literal: When Jin fell into disorder he fled to the lands west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell into turmoil he fled to the lands west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 世祖平涼州，還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang province he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang province he returned home.

sentences.zh: 父擁，字天祐，秦州撫軍府司馬。

translations.literal: His father Yong, courtesy name Tianyou, was staff officer in the Pacification Army headquarters of Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong, courtesy name Tianyou, was staff officer on the Pacification Army staff in Qin province.

sentences.zh: 湛少有器行，頗涉羣書。

translations.literal: Zhan in youth had capacity and conduct and was fairly versed in many books.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan in youth had ability and integrity and read widely.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，舉秀才。

translations.literal: In his twenties he was nominated as Outstanding Talent.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties he was nominated as Outstanding Talent.

sentences.zh: 除奉朝請，領侍御史，轉員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed court attendant and acting attendant censor, then transferred to Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed court attendant and acting attendant censor, then Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤之討關西，以湛為行臺郎中，深見委任。

translations.literal: In Xiao Baoyin's campaign against Guanxi, Zhan served as director on the mobile headquarters and was deeply entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: On Xiao Baoyin's campaign in Guanxi, Zhan served as director on the mobile headquarters and was deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，寶夤大敗東還，朝廷以為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, after Baoyin suffered a great defeat and returned east, the court appointed him governor of Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era, after Baoyin was heavily defeated and retreated east, the court made him governor of Yong province.

sentences.zh: 後自猜懼，害中尉酈道元，乃稱兵反。

translations.literal: Later, in suspicion and fear, he killed the commandant of the palace guards, Li Daoyuan, and then raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Later, growing suspicious and afraid, he killed the commandant of the palace guards Li Daoyuan and raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時湛臥疾於家，寶夤令姜儉報湛云：「元略受蕭衍意旨，乃欲見除。

translations.literal: At that time Zhan was ill at home; Baoyin sent Jiang Jian to report to Zhan, saying, "Yuan Lue received Xiao Yan's intent and means to have me removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was then ill at home; Baoyin sent Jiang Jian to tell him, "Yuan Lue is acting on Xiao Yan's orders and intends to eliminate me.

sentences.zh: 酈道元之來，事不可測。

translations.literal: When Li Daoyuan comes, the affair cannot be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Daoyuan arrives, what will happen cannot be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 吾不能坐受死亡，今便為身計，不復作魏臣也。

translations.literal: I cannot sit and await death; now I must act for my own sake and will no longer be a minister of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot sit and await death; I must now act for my own survival and will no longer serve Wei.

sentences.zh: 與卿契闊，故以相報，死生榮辱，與君共之。」

translations.literal: Our bond is close, so I report this to you—life and death, glory and shame, I share with you."
translations.idiomatic: You and I are close, so I tell you this—life and death, honor and disgrace, we share together."

sentences.zh: 湛聞之，舉聲大哭。

translations.literal: When Zhan heard it he broke into loud weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan heard this he burst into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 儉遽止之曰：「何得便爾？」

translations.literal: Jian hurriedly stopped him, saying, "How can you act so abruptly?"
translations.idiomatic: Jian hurriedly stopped him and said, "How can you react like this?"

sentences.zh: 湛曰：「百口居家，即時屠滅，云何不哭！」

translations.literal: Zhan said, "A household of a hundred mouths will be slaughtered on the spot—how could I not weep!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said, "A household of a hundred souls will be butchered at once—how could I not weep!"

sentences.zh: 哭數十聲，徐謂儉曰：「為我白齊王，王本以窮鳥投人，賴朝廷假王羽翼，榮寵至此。

translations.literal: After weeping several dozen times, he slowly said to Jian, "Tell the Prince of Qi for me: You originally came as a bird at the end of its flight seeking shelter; you relied on the court lending you wings, and came to such glory and favor.
translations.idiomatic: After weeping many times, he slowly told Jian, "Carry this message to the Prince of Qi: You came as a bird at bay seeking refuge; the court lent you wings, and you rose to such honor and favor.

sentences.zh: 屬國步多虞，不能竭忠報德，乃欲乘人間隙，有不臧之心。

translations.literal: Now when the nation's fortunes are full of peril, you cannot exhaust your loyalty to repay virtue, yet wish to seize upon others' gaps, harboring an unrighteous heart.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in peril, yet instead of giving your full loyalty to repay the court's kindness, you mean to exploit others' weakness and harbor an unworthy heart.

sentences.zh: 信惑行路無識之語，欲以羸敗之兵，守關問鼎。

translations.literal: You believe and are misled by the ignorant talk of passersby on the road, wishing with exhausted and defeated troops to hold the passes and contend for the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: You trust the idle gossip of ignorant travelers and mean to hold the passes and seize the throne with broken, defeated troops.

sentences.zh: 今魏德雖衰，天命未改。

translations.literal: Though Wei's virtue has declined, the Mandate of Heaven has not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wei's virtue has waned, Heaven's mandate has not shifted.

sentences.zh: 且王之恩義，未洽於民，但見其敗，未見有成。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Highness's kindness and righteousness have not yet permeated the people—they see only your defeat, not your success.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your kindness and righteousness have not yet won over the people; they have seen only your defeats, not your victories.

sentences.zh: 蘇湛不能以百口居家，為王族滅。」

translations.literal: Su Zhan cannot use a household of a hundred mouths to die for a princely clan."
translations.idiomatic: I, Su Zhan, cannot let my household of a hundred be annihilated for a princely house."

sentences.zh: 寶夤復報曰：「此自救命之計，不得不爾。

translations.literal: Baoyin replied again, "This is a plan to save my own life—I had no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin replied, "This is a plan to save my own life; I had no choice.

sentences.zh: 所以不先相白者，恐沮吾計故爾。」

translations.literal: The reason I did not inform you beforehand was that I feared it would discourage my plan."
translations.idiomatic: I did not tell you beforehand because I feared you would undermine my plan."

sentences.zh: 湛復曰：「凡為大事，當得天下奇士。

translations.literal: Zhan replied again, "Whenever one undertakes a great affair, one must obtain extraordinary men of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan replied, "Any great undertaking requires extraordinary men from across the realm.

sentences.zh: 今但共長安博徒小兒輩計校，辦有成理不？

translations.literal: Now you merely scheme together with the gambling youths of Chang'an—can that succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Now you only plot with the gambling youths of Chang'an—how can that succeed?

sentences.zh: 湛恐荊棘必生庭閤。

translations.literal: Zhan feared that thorns would surely grow in the courtyard hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan feared disaster would surely overtake the household.

sentences.zh: 願乞骸骨還鄉里，脫得因此病死，可以下見先人。」

translations.literal: I wish to request my bones and return to my homeland; if by chance I die of illness because of this, I can go below and meet my forebears."
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to return home with my bones; if I should die of illness because of this, at least I can go below and face my ancestors."

sentences.zh: 寶夤素重之，以湛病，且知不為己用，聽還武功。

translations.literal: Baoyin had always esteemed him; since Zhan was ill and he knew Zhan would not serve him, he allowed him to return to Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin had always held him in esteem; seeing that Zhan was ill and would not serve his cause, he let him return to Wugong.

sentences.zh: 寶夤敗，莊帝即位，徵補尚書郎。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was defeated, Emperor Zhuang took the throne and summoned Zhan to fill the post of Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoyin was defeated, Emperor Zhuang took the throne and summoned Zhan to serve as Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 既至，莊帝曰：「前聞卿答蕭寶夤，甚有美辭，為我說也。」

translations.literal: When he arrived, Emperor Zhuang said, "I heard earlier that your reply to Xiao Baoyin had very fine words—tell me about it."
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Emperor Zhuang said, "I heard your reply to Xiao Baoyin was eloquent indeed—tell me about it."

sentences.zh: 湛頓首謝曰：「臣雖言辭不如伍被，始終不易，自謂過之。

translations.literal: Zhan kowtowed and said, "Though my words are not equal to Wu Bei's, in remaining unchanged from beginning to end I believe I surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan kowtowed and said, "Though my eloquence does not match Wu Bei's, in holding firm from start to finish I believe I surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 然臣與寶夤周遊契闊，言得盡心，而不能令其不反，臣之罪也。」

translations.literal: Yet I traveled with Baoyin through hardship and spoke with all my heart, yet could not make him not rebel—this is my crime."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I traveled with Baoyin through hardship and spoke with all my heart, yet could not keep him from rebellion—that is my fault."

sentences.zh: 莊帝悅，拜散騎都尉，仍領郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and appointed him Commandant of Scattered Cavalry, while retaining his master of writing post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and appointed him Commandant of Scattered Cavalry while retaining his post as Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Attendant at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Attendant at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，病還鄉里，終於家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign, he fell ill and returned home, dying at his house.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Chu's reign he fell ill, returned home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、鎮西將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Regular Attendant Cavalier, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant Cavalier, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 湛從母弟天水姜儉，字文簡。

translations.literal: Zhan's younger maternal cousin Jiang Jian of Tianshui, courtesy name Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's younger maternal cousin Jiang Jian of Tianshui, courtesy name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 父昭，自平憲司直，出為兗州安東長史，帶高平太守，卒於營構都將。

translations.literal: His father Zhao rose from rectifier in the Directorate of Fair Administration to Longitudinal Staff Officer on the Eastern Pacification staff in Yan province, concurrently serving as administrator of Gaoping, and died while serving as Commissioned General for Camp Construction.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao rose from rectifier in the Directorate of Fair Administration to Longitudinal Staff Officer on the Eastern Pacification staff in Yan province, concurrently administrator of Gaoping, and died while serving as Commissioned General for Camp Construction.

sentences.zh: 儉少有幹用，勤濟過人。

translations.literal: Jian from youth had capacity and usefulness, and diligence exceeding others.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jian had ability and drive, and his diligence surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 起家徐州車騎府田曹參軍，轉太尉外兵參軍。

translations.literal: He began as Military Staff Officer for Agriculture in the chariots and cavalry headquarters of Xu province, then transferred to Outside Troops Staff Officer under the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Military Staff Officer for Agriculture in the chariots and cavalry headquarters of Xu province, then transferred to Outside Troops Staff Officer under the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤出討關西，引為開府屬，軍機謀略，多所參預。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin went out to campaign in Guanxi, he recruited Jian as staff member of his headquarters; in military plans and strategy Jian participated extensively.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin marched west to campaign in Guanxi, he recruited Jian as staff member of his headquarters, and Jian took part extensively in military planning and strategy.

sentences.zh: 儉亦自謂遭逢知己，遂竭誠委託。

translations.literal: Jian also considered himself to have met a true appreciator and so devoted himself wholeheartedly.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also believed he had found a true patron and gave himself over wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 寶夤為雍州，仍請為開府從事中郎，帶長安令。

translations.literal: When Baoyin became governor of Yong province, he still requested Jian as Senior Clerk in the headquarters staff, concurrently Chief Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin became governor of Yong province, he again requested Jian as Senior Clerk on his headquarters staff, concurrently Chief Magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤反，以為左丞，尤見信任，為羣下所讎疾。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled, Jian was made Left Assistant and especially trusted, but hated by the other subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled, Jian was made Left Assistant and especially trusted, but the other subordinates resented and hated him.

sentences.zh: 寶夤敗，城人殺之，時年三十九。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was defeated, the people of the city killed him; he was thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was defeated, the people of the city killed him; he was thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 蘇湛每謂人曰：「以姜儉才志，堪致富貴。

translations.literal: Su Zhan often told people, "Given Jiang Jian's talent and ambition, he could have attained wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhan often told people, "Given Jiang Jian's talent and ambition, he could have attained wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 惜其不遇，命也如何！」

translations.literal: Pity that he did not meet with success—such is fate, what can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Pity that he never found his opportunity—such is fate; what can one do?"

sentences.zh: 儉弟素，武定末，中散大夫。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Su, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Regular Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Su, at the end of the Wuding era, served as Regular Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 杜銓，字士衡，京兆人。

translations.literal: Du Quan, courtesy name Shiheng, was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Quan, courtesy name Shiheng, was a man of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 晉征南將軍預五世孫也。

translations.literal: He was fifth-generation descendant of Du Yu, Jin's General Who Conquers the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fifth-generation descendant of Du Yu, Jin's General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 祖冑，苻堅太尉長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhou was Longitudinal Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant under Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhou served Fu Jian as Longitudinal Staff Officer to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 父嶷，慕容垂祕書監，仍僑居趙郡。

translations.literal: His father Ni served Murong Chui as Director of the Secretariat, and remained sojourning in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ni served Murong Chui as Director of the Secretariat and continued to live as a sojourner in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 銓學涉有長者風，與盧玄、高允等同被徵為中書博士。

translations.literal: Quan was broadly learned with the air of an elder gentleman; along with Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and others he was summoned to serve as Erudite at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was broadly learned and had the bearing of an elder gentleman; along with Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and others he was summoned to serve as Erudite at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，密太后父豹喪在濮陽，世祖欲命迎葬於鄴，謂司徒崔浩曰：「天下諸杜，何處望高？」

translations.literal: Initially, Empress Dowager Mi's father's coffin was in Puyang; Emperor Shizu wished to have it brought for burial at Ye and said to the Minister of Public Works Cui Hao, "Among all the Du clans under Heaven, where is the most prestigious lineage?"
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Empress Dowager Mi's father's coffin lay in Puyang; Emperor Shizu wished to have it brought for burial at Ye and said to the Minister of Public Works Cui Hao, "Among all the Du clans under Heaven, which lineage ranks highest?"

sentences.zh: 浩對京兆為美。

translations.literal: Hao replied that Jingzhao was the finest.
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied that Jingzhao was the finest.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「朕今方改葬外祖，意欲取京兆中長老一人，[5]以為宗正，命營護凶事。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu said, "I am now about to rebury my maternal grandfather and wish to take one elder from Jingzhao [5] to serve as Director of the Imperial Clan and charge him with overseeing the funeral rites."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu said, "I am now about to rebury my maternal grandfather and wish to select one elder from Jingzhao [5] to serve as Director of the Imperial Clan and put him in charge of the funeral rites."

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「中書博士杜銓，其家今在趙郡，是杜預之後，於今為諸杜之最，即可取之。」

translations.literal: Hao said, "Erudite at the Secretariat Du Quan—his family is now in Zhao commandery; he is a descendant of Du Yu and is today foremost among all the Du, so he may be selected."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Erudite at the Secretariat Du Quan—his family is now in Zhao commandery; he is a descendant of Du Yu and is today foremost among all the Du clans, so he should be chosen."

sentences.zh: 詔召見。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him for an audience.

sentences.zh: 銓器貌瓌雅，世祖感悅，謂浩曰：「此真吾所欲也。」

translations.literal: Quan's bearing and appearance were splendid and elegant; Emperor Shizu was moved and pleased, and said to Hao, "This is truly what I wanted."
translations.idiomatic: Quan's bearing and appearance were splendid and elegant; Emperor Shizu was delighted and said to Hao, "This is exactly what I wanted."

sentences.zh: 以為宗正，令與杜超子道生迎豹喪柩，致葬鄴南。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan and ordered together with Du Chao's son Daosheng to meet the coffin of Bao and conduct burial south of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan and ordered, together with Du Chao's son Daosheng, to meet Bao's coffin and conduct the burial south of Ye.

sentences.zh: 銓遂與超如親。

translations.literal: Quan and Chao thereupon became as close as kin.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and Chao thereupon became as close as kin.

sentences.zh: 超謂銓曰：「既是宗近，何緣復僑居趙郡？」

translations.literal: Chao said to Quan, "Since we are close in the clan, why do you still sojourn in Zhao commandery?"
translations.idiomatic: Chao said to Quan, "Since we are close in the clan, why do you still live as a sojourner in Zhao commandery?"

sentences.zh: 乃迎引同屬魏郡焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he brought him to join the clan register in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he brought him to join the clan register in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎侍郎，轉中書侍郎，賜爵新豐侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Cavalier, then transferred to Attendant at the Secretariat, and was granted the title Marquis of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Cavalier, then transferred to Attendant at the Secretariat, and was granted the title Marquis of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平南將軍、相州刺史，魏縣侯，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Xiang province, Marquis of Wei county, with posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Xiang province, and Marquis of Wei county, with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子振，字季元。

translations.literal: His son Zhen, courtesy name Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen, courtesy name Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太和初，舉秀才，卒於中書博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was nominated as Outstanding Talent and died while serving as Erudite at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe he was nominated as Outstanding Talent and died while serving as Erudite at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子遇，字慶期。

translations.literal: His son Yu, courtesy name Qingqi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu, courtesy name Qingqi.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: He began his career as court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as court attendant.

sentences.zh: 轉員外散騎侍郎、尚書起部郎中。

translations.literal: He transferred to Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and Director in the Ministry of Works for Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and Director in the Ministry of Works for Construction.

sentences.zh: 竊官材瓦起立私宅，清論鄙之。

translations.literal: He stole official timber and tiles to build a private residence; purists held him in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: He stole official timber and tiles to build a private residence, and men of principle held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Flying Dragon and Regular Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Flying Dragon and Regular Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 出為河東太守。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈中軍將軍、都官尚書、豫州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously honored as General of the Central Army, Minister of Justice, Governor of Yu province, with posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as General of the Central Army, Minister of Justice, and Governor of Yu province, with the posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 子鴻，永熙中，司徒倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Hong, during the Yongxi era, served as Military Staff Officer for Granaries on the Minister of Public Works staff.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong, during the Yongxi era, served as Military Staff Officer for Granaries on the Minister of Public Works staff.

sentences.zh: 銓族子洪太，字道廓。

translations.literal: Quan's clansman Hong Tai, courtesy name Daokuo.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's clansman Hong Tai, courtesy name Daokuo.

sentences.zh: 延興中為中書博士。
