translations.literal: During the Yansing era he served as Erudite at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yansing era he served as Erudite at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後使高麗，除安遠將軍、下邳太守，轉梁郡太守。

translations.literal: Later he was sent to Goguryeo, appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and administrator of Xiapi, then transferred to administrator of Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was sent on mission to Goguryeo, appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and administrator of Xiapi, then transferred to administrator of Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 太和中，除鷹揚將軍、絳城鎮將，帶新昌、陽平二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was appointed General of the Soaring Hawk and garrison commander of Jiangcheng, concurrently administrator of Xinchang and Yangping commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he was appointed General of the Soaring Hawk and garrison commander of Jiangcheng, concurrently administrator of Xinchang and Yangping commanderies.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 子祖悅，字士豁，頗有識尚。

translations.literal: His son Zuyue, courtesy name Shihuo, had considerable insight and aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuyue, courtesy name Shihuo, had considerable insight and aspiration.

sentences.zh: 大將軍劉昶參軍事，稍遷天水、仇池二郡太守，行南秦州事。

translations.literal: He served as staff officer on Grand General Liu Chang's staff, gradually promoted to administrator of both Tianshui and Qiuchi commanderies, acting governor of Southern Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer on Grand General Liu Chang's staff, gradually promoted to administrator of both Tianshui and Qiuchi commanderies, and acted as governor of Southern Qin province.

sentences.zh: 正光中，入為太尉、汝南王悅諮議參軍。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguang era he entered the capital as advisory staff officer to the Grand Commandant and Prince of Runan Yuan Yue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era he entered the capital as advisory staff officer to the Grand Commandant and Prince of Runan Yuan Yue.

sentences.zh: 出除高陽太守，卒於郡。

translations.literal: He went out and was appointed administrator of Gaoyang; he died in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He went out and was appointed administrator of Gaoyang, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子長文，字子儒。

translations.literal: His son Changwen, courtesy name Ziru.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changwen, courtesy name Ziru.

sentences.zh: 肅宗挽郎、員外散騎侍郎，稍遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: Bearer at Emperor Suzong's funeral, Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier, gradually promoted to Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as bearer at Emperor Suzong's funeral and as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier, then gradually rose to Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 以隨叔顒守岐州勳，賜爵始平伯，加平東將軍。

translations.literal: For following his uncle Yan in defending Qizhou he was granted the title Baron of Shiping and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: For following his uncle Yan in defending Qizhou he was granted the title Baron of Shiping and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 天平末，卒於安西將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianping he died while serving as General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianping he died while serving as General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 贈中軍將軍、度支尚書、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as General of the Central Army, Minister of Revenue, and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of the Central Army, Minister of Revenue, and Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 長文第四弟子達，武定中，齊文襄王大都督府戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: Changwen's fourth younger brother Zida, during the Wuding era served as Military Staff Officer for Households in the grand chief commander headquarters of Prince Wenxiang of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Changwen's fourth younger brother Zida, during the Wuding era served as Military Staff Officer for Households in the grand chief commander headquarters of Prince Wenxiang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 祖悅弟顒，字思顏，頗有幹用。

translations.literal: Zuyue's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Siyan, had considerable capacity and usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyue's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Siyan, had considerable capacity and usefulness.

sentences.zh: 解褐北中府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the cloth he served as Recording Staff Officer in the Northern Center headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving the cloth he served as Recording Staff Officer in the Northern Center headquarters.

sentences.zh: 正光中，稍遷厲威將軍、盱眙太守，帶大徐戍主。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguang era he was gradually promoted to General Who Inspires Awe, administrator of Xuyi, concurrently commander of the great Xu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era he was gradually promoted to General Who Inspires Awe, administrator of Xuyi, concurrently commander of the great Xu garrison.

sentences.zh: 元法僧之叛也，顒逃竄獲免。

translations.literal: When Yuan Faseng rebelled, Yan fled and escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng rebelled, Yan fled and escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 後為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Later he served as Grand Master for Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Grand Master for Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年，為西征軍司，行岐州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaochang he served as army director on the Western Expedition and acted as governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaochang he served as army director on the Western Expedition and acted as governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤起逆，顒據州不從。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin rose in rebellion, Yan held the province and refused to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin rose in rebellion, Yan held the province and refused to follow him.

sentences.zh: 還，除征虜將軍、東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Eastern Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Eastern Jing province.

sentences.zh: 以守岐州勳，封平陽縣開國伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For the merit of defending Qizhou he was enfeoffed as Baron with a state of five hundred households at Pingyang county.
translations.idiomatic: For the merit of defending Qizhou he was enfeoffed as founding Baron of Pingyang county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 武泰中，轉授岐州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Wutai era he was transferred and given the governorship of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wutai era he was transferred and appointed Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 永安中，除涇州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Yong'an era he was appointed governor of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era he was appointed Governor of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 時万俟醜奴充斥關右，不行。

translations.literal: At that time Moqi Chounu filled Guanxi; he could not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Moqi Chounu filled Guanxi, and he could not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 乃為都督，防守岐州。

translations.literal: He therefore served as area commander defending Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore served as area commander defending Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 醜奴攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Chounu attacked him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu attacked him but could not overcome him.

sentences.zh: 事寧，除鎮西將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When affairs settled he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs settled he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 以勳又賞安平縣開國伯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was additionally rewarded with a state of five hundred households as Baron with a state at Anping county.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was additionally rewarded as founding Baron of Anping county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 以平陽伯轉授弟二子景仲。

translations.literal: He transferred the Pingyang baroncy to his second son Jingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred the Pingyang baroncy to his second son Jingzhong.

sentences.zh: 後為征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫，沒於關西。

translations.literal: Later he served as General Who Conquers the West and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and died in Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as General Who Conquers the West and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and died in Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 裴駿，字神駒，小名皮，河東聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Jun, courtesy name Shenju, childhood name Pi, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun, courtesy name Shenju, childhood name Pi, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父雙碩，本縣令，假建威將軍、恒農太守，安邑子。

translations.literal: His father Shuangshuo was magistrate of his home county, acting General Who Establishes Might and administrator of Hengnong, Viscount of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuangshuo was magistrate of his home county, acting General Who Establishes Might and administrator of Hengnong, and Viscount of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平南將軍、東雍州刺史，聞喜侯。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Eastern Yong province, and Marquis of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Eastern Yong province, and Marquis of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 駿幼而聰慧，親表異之，稱為「神駒」，因以為字。

translations.literal: Jun from childhood was intelligent; relatives and cousins regarded him as extraordinary and called him "Divine Colt," which became his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was intelligent from childhood; relatives and cousins marveled at him and called him "Divine Colt," which became his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，通涉經史，好屬文，性方檢，有禮度，鄉里宗敬焉。

translations.literal: At his coming of age he was broadly versed in the classics and histories, loved composing literary pieces, and was upright and restrained in nature with proper decorum; his district revered and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: At his coming of age he was broadly versed in the classics and histories, loved composing literary pieces, and was upright and restrained by nature with proper decorum; his district revered and respected him.

sentences.zh: 蓋吳作亂於關中，汾陰人薛永宗聚眾應之，屢殘破諸縣，來襲聞喜。

translations.literal: Gai Wu rebelled in Guanzhong; Xue Yongzong of Fenyin gathered a force in response, repeatedly ravaging the counties, and came to attack Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Wu raised rebellion in Guanzhong; Xue Yongzong of Fenyin rallied followers in support, repeatedly raiding and ravaging the counties, and marched to attack Wenxi.

sentences.zh: [6]縣中先無兵仗，人情駭動，縣令憂惶，計無所出。

translations.literal: [6] The county had no weapons at first; popular sentiment was alarmed and shaken; the magistrate was anxious and frightened and could think of no plan.
translations.idiomatic: [6] The county had no arms on hand; the people were terrified; the magistrate was stricken with fear and could think of no recourse.

sentences.zh: 駿在家聞之，便率厲鄉豪曰：「在禮，君父有危，臣子致命。

translations.literal: Jun at home heard of it and straightaway rallied the district magnates, saying: "By the rites, when lord and father are in peril, ministers and sons should give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun heard the news at home, he immediately rallied the local leaders and said, "By the rites, when lord and father are in danger, ministers and sons must give their lives.

sentences.zh: 府縣今為賊所逼，是吾等徇節之秋。

translations.literal: The prefecture and county are now pressed by bandits—this is our season to devote ourselves to duty.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture and county are now besieged by rebels—this is the hour for us to prove our loyalty.

sentences.zh: 諸君可不勉乎！」

translations.literal: Gentlemen, can you not exert yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Will you not do your utmost, gentlemen!

sentences.zh: 諸豪皆奮激請行，駿乃簡騎驍勇數百人奔赴。

translations.literal: All the magnates were stirred and eager to go; Jun then selected several hundred fierce and brave horsemen and hastened there.
translations.idiomatic: All the leaders leapt forward with ardor, begging to go; Jun then chose several hundred of the bravest horsemen and rode to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 賊聞救至，引兵退走。

translations.literal: The bandits, hearing that relief had arrived, withdrew their troops and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels learned that relief had arrived, they withdrew and fled.

sentences.zh: 刺史嘉之，以狀表聞。

translations.literal: The inspector commended him and reported the matter by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial inspector commended his action and reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 會世祖親討蓋吳，引見駿，駿陳敍事宜，甚會機理。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Shizu personally campaigned against Gai Wu, summoned Jun for audience; Jun set forth the affairs of the day, very much in accord with the logic of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Emperor Shizu was personally campaigning against Gai Wu; he summoned Jun for an audience, and Jun expounded on the matters at hand with excellent judgment and insight.

sentences.zh: 世祖大悅，顧謂崔浩曰：「裴駿有當世才具，且忠義可嘉。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu was greatly pleased and, turning, said to Cui Hao: "Pei Jun possesses talents for our age, and his loyalty and righteousness are admirable."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was greatly pleased and, turning to Cui Hao, said, "Pei Jun has the capacity for leadership in our time, and his loyalty and righteousness are worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 補中書博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed supplemental Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 浩亦深器駿，目為三河領袖。

translations.literal: Hao also greatly valued Jun and regarded him as a leader of the Three Rivers region.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also held Jun in deep esteem and looked on him as a leader of the Three Rivers region.

sentences.zh: 轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 劉駿遣使明僧暠朝貢，以駿有才學，乃假給事中、散騎常侍，於境上勞接。

translations.literal: Liu Jun sent the envoy Ming Senghao to offer tribute at court; because Jun had talent and learning, he was provisionally given the posts of Palatial Attendant and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, to receive and entertain them at the border.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun of Song sent the envoy Ming Senghao to pay tribute at court; because Jun was gifted in scholarship, he was given provisional appointment as Palatial Attendant and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry to receive and entertain the envoy at the border.

sentences.zh: 皇興二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Huangxing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Huangxing era.

sentences.zh: 贈平南將軍、秦州刺史、聞喜侯，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Qin province, and Marquis of Wenxi; posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Qin province, and Marquis of Wenxi, with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 子修，字元寄，清辯好學。

translations.literal: His son Xiu, courtesy name Yuanji, was lucid in debate and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiu, courtesy name Yuanji, was clear in argument and devoted to study.

sentences.zh: 年十三，補中書學生，遷祕書中散，轉主客令。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he was appointed student of the Secretariat, promoted to Disperser of the Secretariat, and transferred to Director of Receiving Guests.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he entered service as a Secretariat student, was promoted to Disperser of the Secretariat, and then transferred to Director of Receiving Guests.

sentences.zh: 以婦父李訢事，出為張掖子都大將。

translations.literal: On account of the affair of his wife's father Li Xin, he was sent out as Major General of the Ziye Garrison at Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the affair involving his father-in-law Li Xin, he was dispatched as Major General of the Ziye Garrison at Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 張掖境接胡夷，前後數致寇掠，修明設烽候，以方略禦之。

translations.literal: Zhangye's borders adjoined the Hu and Yi peoples; before and after they had repeatedly caused raids and plunder; Xiu made clear the beacon posts and defended against them by strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangye's frontier bordered the barbarian tribes, which had repeatedly raided the region; Xiu established beacon posts and used strategic measures to defend against them.

sentences.zh: 在邊六年，關塞清靜。

translations.literal: On the frontier for six years, the passes and defiles were peaceful and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the frontier for six years, and the border passes remained secure and tranquil.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，徵為中部令。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu commended him and summoned him as Prefect of Zhongbu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu praised his service and summoned him to serve as Prefect of Zhongbu.

sentences.zh: 轉中大夫，兼祠部曹事，職主禮樂，每有疑議，修斟酌故實，咸有條貫。

translations.literal: Transferred to Grand Master of the Palace, concurrently in charge of the Bureau of Sacrifice affairs; his duty was rites and music; whenever doubts arose, Xiu weighed precedents and actual cases, all with coherent order.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Palace and concurrently placed in charge of the Sacrifices Bureau, overseeing rites and music; whenever questions arose, Xiu weighed historical precedents, and his decisions were always systematic and well founded.

sentences.zh: 太和十六年卒，時年五十一。

translations.literal: He died in the sixteenth year of Taihe, aged fifty-one at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year of the Taihe era, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 高祖悼惜之，賻帛一百匹，諡曰恭伯。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu mourned and regretted him, bestowing one hundred bolts of silk as funeral gift; posthumous title Gongbo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu grieved his loss and bestowed one hundred bolts of silk as funeral gifts; his posthumous title was Gongbo.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，追贈輔國將軍、東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Shizong, posthumously honored as General Who Assists the State and Governor of Eastern Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he was posthumously promoted to General Who Assists the State and Governor of Eastern Qin province.

sentences.zh: 修早孤，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xiu was orphaned early; in mourning he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu lost his father early and won renown for filial devotion during the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 二弟三妹並在幼弱，撫養訓誨，甚有義方。

translations.literal: Two younger brothers and three younger sisters were all still young and weak; he reared, nurtured, and instructed them, with very proper moral guidance.
translations.idiomatic: With two younger brothers and three younger sisters still in their infancy, he raised and instructed them with exemplary moral discipline.

sentences.zh: 次弟務早喪，修哀傷之，感於行路。

translations.literal: His next younger brother Wu died early; Xiu grieved for him, moving those on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When his next younger brother Wu died young, Xiu's grief was so profound that it moved all who passed by.

sentences.zh: 愛育孤姪，同於己子。

translations.literal: He cherished and reared his orphaned nephew as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: He lovingly raised his orphaned nephew as though the boy were his own son.

sentences.zh: 及將異居，奴婢田宅悉推與之，時人以此稱焉。

translations.literal: When they were about to live separately, he turned over all slaves, servants, fields, and houses to them; people of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to set up separate households, he gave his siblings all the slaves, fields, and dwellings; people of the time praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 子詢，字敬叔。

translations.literal: His son Xun, courtesy name Jingshu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun, courtesy name Jingshu.

sentences.zh: 美儀貌，多藝能，音律博弈，咸所開解。

translations.literal: Handsome in bearing and appearance, with many talents; in music, ball games, and board games, all were understood by him.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome in bearing and possessed many talents; he was equally proficient in music, ball games, and board games.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請，太尉集曹參軍，轉長流尚書起部郎中、平昌太守。

translations.literal: He first entered service as Attendant at the Court, staff officer of the Collecting Bureau on the staff of the Grand Commandant, transferred to Departmental Attendant of the Initiation Bureau in the Flowing Chief Ministry and administrator of Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Attendant at Court, served as staff officer of the Collecting Bureau on the Grand Commandant's staff, and was transferred to Departmental Attendant of the Initiation Bureau and administrator of Pingchang commandery.

sentences.zh: 時太原長公主寡居，與詢私姦，肅宗仍詔詢尚焉。

translations.literal: At the time the Princess of Taiyuan was living in widowhood; she had a secret affair with Xun; Emperor Suzong then ordered Xun to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Taiyuan was then living as a widow; she and Xun entered into a secret affair, and Emperor Suzong subsequently commanded Xun to marry her.

sentences.zh: 尋以主壻，特除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon, as the princess's son-in-law, he was specially appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as the emperor's son-in-law, he was specially appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時本邑中正闕，司徒召詢為之。

translations.literal: At the time the district Rectifier for his native commandery was vacant; the Minister of Education summoned Xun to fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: When the district Rectifier for his native commandery fell vacant, the Minister of Education appointed Xun to the post.

sentences.zh: 詢族叔昞自陳情願此官，詢遂讓焉，時論善之。

translations.literal: Xun's clansman and uncle Bing personally stated his wish for this office; Xun then yielded it to him, and opinion of the day praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's clansman and uncle Bing expressed his desire for the office; Xun yielded it to him, and contemporary opinion praised his generosity.

sentences.zh: 尋監起居事，遷祕書監。

translations.literal: Soon he supervised the Affairs of the Rise and Rest, and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of recording the imperial diary and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為平南將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Sent out as General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched as General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 詢以凡司戍主蠻酋田朴特地居要險，[7]眾踰數萬，足為邊捍，遂表朴特為西郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Xun, because the Yefan garrison commander, the barbarian chieftain Tian Putie, occupied a strategically crucial and perilous position, [7] with followers exceeding tens of thousands, sufficient to serve as frontier defense, memorialized to appoint Putie as Governor of Western Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: Xun noted that Tian Putie, chieftain of the Yefan garrison, held a strategically vital and defensible position [7] with a following of tens of thousands—enough to guard the frontier—and memorialized to appoint Putie Governor of Western Ying province.

sentences.zh: 朝議許之。

translations.literal: Court deliberation approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將李國興寇邊，時四方多事，朝廷未遑外略，緣境城戍，多為國興所陷。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent the general Li Guoxing to raid the border; at the time the four quarters had many affairs; the court had no leisure for external strategy; border garrisons along the frontier were mostly captured by Guoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent the general Li Guoxing to raid the border; with troubles on all sides, the court had no leisure for external campaigns, and many frontier garrisons along the border fell to Guoxing.

sentences.zh: 賊既乘勝，遂向州城。

translations.literal: The bandits, having seized the momentum of victory, then pressed toward the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by their victories, the rebels then marched on the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 詢率厲固守，垂將百日，援軍既至，賊乃退走。

translations.literal: Xun rallied and encouraged steadfast defense; it approached one hundred days; relief troops having arrived, the bandits then withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xun rallied the garrison in a resolute defense; after nearly a hundred days relief forces arrived, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍、安南將軍。

translations.literal: Promoted additionally as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 朴特自國興來寇，便與詢掎角，為表裏聲援，郢州獲全，朴特頗有力焉。

translations.literal: From the time Guoxing came raiding, Putie coordinated with Xun in pincer fashion, providing mutual support inside and out; Ying province was preserved intact, and Putie contributed considerable strength to this.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment Guoxing launched his invasion, Putie coordinated with Xun in a pincer movement, providing mutual support; Ying province was saved largely through Putie's efforts.

sentences.zh: 徵為七兵尚書，至都未幾，除豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Summoned as Minister of the Seven Troops; having reached the capital not long, appointed Governor of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as Minister of the Seven Troops; shortly after arriving he was appointed Governor of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 尋進號撫軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the Army, additionally Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 未之州，還為七兵尚書，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Before going to the province, he returned as Minister of the Seven Troops, Regular Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his post in Yu province, he was recalled to serve again as Minister of the Seven Troops, retaining his title of Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武泰初，詔詢以本官兼侍中，為關右大使，賞擢慕義之徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wutai, an edict ordered Xun, in his original office concurrently as Palace Attendant, to serve as envoy to the Guanxi region, rewarding and promoting those who yearned for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wutai era an edict appointed Xun, retaining his existing rank while concurrently serving as Palace Attendant, as envoy to the Guanxi region to reward those who had come over in allegiance.

sentences.zh: 未及發，會尒朱榮入洛，於河陰遇害，年五十一。

translations.literal: Before he had set out, it happened that Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang; at Heyin he met with violent death, aged fifty-one at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang; Xun was killed at Heyin, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、車騎大將軍、司空公、雍州刺史，諡曰貞烈。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of Excellency of Works, and Governor of Yong province; posthumous title Zhenlie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of the Excellency of Works, and Governor of Yong province, with the posthumous title Zhenlie.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

sentences.zh: 修弟務，字陽仁，少而聰慧。

translations.literal: Xiu's younger brother Wu, courtesy name Yangren, from youth was intelligent and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's younger brother Wu, courtesy name Yangren, was intelligent from youth.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: Selected as Filial-and-Incorrupt candidate; the province summoned him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as a Filial-and-Incorrupt candidate and summoned by the province to serve as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: Died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 子美，字師伯，少有美名。

translations.literal: His son Mei, courtesy name Shibo, from youth had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mei, courtesy name Shibo, enjoyed an excellent reputation from youth.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，州主簿。

translations.literal: Selected as Filial-and-Incorrupt candidate; provincial Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as a Filial-and-Incorrupt candidate and served as provincial Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 太尉咸陽王雅相賞愛，欲以女妻之，美拒而不納。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant, Prince of Xianyang, Wang Ya, admired and loved him, wishing to give him his daughter in marriage; Mei refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya, Prince of Xianyang and Grand Commandant, admired him and wished to marry his daughter to him, but Mei refused.

sentences.zh: 除奉朝請，亦早卒。

translations.literal: Appointed Attendant at Court; also died early.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant at Court but likewise died young.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

sentences.zh: 務弟宣，字叔令，通辯博物，早有聲譽。

translations.literal: Wu's younger brother Xuan, courtesy name Shuling, was fluent in debate and broadly learned, early attaining reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's younger brother Xuan, courtesy name Shuling, was eloquent and widely learned, and earned an early reputation.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母兄以孝友稱。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth; in serving his mother and elder brother he was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was renowned for filial devotion toward his mother and cordial affection toward his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，至都，見司空李訢，與言自旦及夕，訢嗟善不已。

translations.literal: Selected as Filial-and-Incorrupt candidate; upon reaching the capital, he met the Excellency of Works Li Xin; conversing from dawn till evening, Xin sighed in admiration without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a Filial-and-Incorrupt candidate, he went to the capital and met Li Xin, Excellency of Works; they talked from dawn till dusk, and Xin expressed unending admiration.

sentences.zh: 司空李沖有人倫鑒識，見而重之。

translations.literal: The Excellency of Works Li Chong had discernment in human affairs; upon seeing him he held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Excellency of Works, was a keen judge of character; when he met Xuan he held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，徵為尚書主客郎，與蕭賾使顏幼明、劉思效、蕭琛、范雲等對接。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign, summoned as Secretary of Receiving Guests in the Ministry of State; he received and entertained Xiao Ze's envoys Yan Youming, Liu Sixiao, Xiao Chen, Fan Yun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign he was summoned to serve as Secretary of Receiving Guests in the Ministry of State, where he received Xiao Ze's envoys Yan Youming, Liu Sixiao, Xiao Chen, Fan Yun, and others.

sentences.zh: 轉都官郎，遷員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Transferred to Secretary of the Capital; promoted to Outer Supplementary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Secretary of the Capital and promoted to Outer Supplementary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: [8]舊令與吏部郎同班。

translations.literal: [8] By old regulation he shared rank with the Secretary of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: [8] By former regulation he shared the same rank as the Secretary of the Ministry of Personnel.

translations.literal: 〈Lacuna.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Lacuna.〉

sentences.zh: 高祖曾集沙門講佛經，因命宣論難，甚有理詣，高祖稱善。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu once gathered Buddhist monks to expound the sutras; he then ordered Xuan to debate doctrine; his reasoning was very apt; Emperor Gaozu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu once assembled Buddhist monks to expound the sutras and then ordered Xuan to engage in doctrinal debate; Xuan's reasoning was excellent, and the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 遷都洛陽，以宣為採材副將。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, Xuan was appointed Deputy General for Timber Procurement.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was relocated to Luoyang, Xuan was appointed Deputy General for Timber Procurement.

sentences.zh: 奉使稱旨，遙除司空諮議參軍。

translations.literal: On mission he fulfilled the imperial intent; from afar appointed advisory staff officer on the staff of the Excellency of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His mission fulfilled the emperor's wishes, and he was appointed from afar as advisory staff officer on the staff of the Excellency of Works.

sentences.zh: 府解，轉司州治中，兼司徒右長史，又轉別駕，仍長史。

translations.literal: When the bureau was dissolved, transferred to Administrative Assistant of Si province, concurrently Senior Clerk on the right of the Minister of Education; again transferred to Vice Administrator, still Senior Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When that office was abolished, he became Administrative Assistant of Si province and concurrently Senior Clerk on the right staff of the Minister of Education; he was then transferred to Vice Administrator while continuing as Senior Clerk.

sentences.zh: 宣明敏有器幹，總攝州府，事無凝滯，遠近稱之。

translations.literal: Xuan was bright, keen, and endowed with capacity; he oversaw the province and prefecture as a whole; affairs had no stagnation; near and far praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was intelligent, capable, and quick-witted; he directed provincial and prefectural affairs without delay, and won praise throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，除太中大夫，領本郡中正，仍別駕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong, appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel, concurrently Rectifier for his native commandery, still Vice Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel and concurrently served as Rectifier for his native commandery while continuing as Vice Administrator.

sentences.zh: 又為司州都督，遷太尉長史。

translations.literal: Again served as Area Commander of Si province; promoted to Senior Clerk on the staff of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Area Commander of Si province and was promoted to Senior Clerk on the Grand Commandant's staff.

sentences.zh: 宣上言曰：「自遷都已來，凡戰陳之處，及軍罷兵還之道，所有骸骼無人覆藏者，請悉令州郡戍邏檢行埋掩。

translations.literal: Xuan submitted a memorial saying: "Since the relocation of the capital, wherever battle has been joined and on the roads by which armies have withdrawn and returned, wherever skeletal remains lie without anyone to cover and bury them, I ask that all be ordered that garrisons and prefectures and commanderies patrol, inspect, and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan submitted a memorial: "Since the capital was moved, wherever battles have been fought and along the roads where armies have marched and withdrawn, wherever human remains lie unburied, I ask that garrisons in every province and commandery be ordered to search for and bury them.

sentences.zh: 并符出兵之鄉：其家有死於戎役者，使皆招魂復魄，祔祭先靈，復其年租調；

translations.literal: Also issue orders to the districts from which troops were levied: for families with members who died on campaign, have them all summon back the souls and restore the spirits, perform supplementary sacrifice to the ancestral spirits, and remit their annual land tax and corvée levies;
translations.idiomatic: Also issue orders to the districts that supplied troops: for families who lost members in military service, have them perform rites to recall the spirits of the dead and offer sacrifice at the ancestral shrine, and remit their annual land tax and corvée levies;

sentences.zh: 身被傷痍者，免其兵役。」

translations.literal: For those personally wounded or maimed, exempt them from military service."
translations.idiomatic: Those who were wounded in body shall be exempt from military service.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 出為征虜將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: Sent out as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Yi province.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Yi province.

sentences.zh: 宣善於綏撫，甚得羌戎之心。

translations.literal: Xuan was skilled at comforting and winning over; he greatly won the hearts of the Qiang and Rong peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan excelled at winning people over through gentle governance and won the deep loyalty of the Qiang and Rong peoples.

sentences.zh: 復晉壽，更置益州，改宣所莅為南秦州。

translations.literal: Jingshou was recovered; Yi province was re-established at a new site; the area where Xuan had governed was changed to Southern Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingshou was recovered, Yi province was re-established elsewhere, and the territory Xuan had governed was redesignated Southern Qin province.

sentences.zh: 先是，有陰平氐酋楊孟孫，擁戶數萬，自立為王，通引蕭衍，數為邊患。

translations.literal: Earlier, there was the Yinping Di chieftain Yang Mengsun, controlling households numbering in the tens of thousands, who set himself up as king, maintained contact with and drew in Xiao Yan, and repeatedly caused border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Yinping Di chieftain Yang Mengsun had gathered tens of thousands of households, declared himself king, maintained ties with Xiao Yan, and repeatedly menaced the frontier.

sentences.zh: 宣乃遣使招喻，曉以逆順，孟孫感恩，即遣子詣闕。

translations.literal: Xuan then sent envoys to summon and instruct him, making clear the way of rebellion and submission; Mengsun was grateful and straightaway sent his son to audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent envoys to win him over, explaining the consequences of rebellion and submission; grateful, Mengsun immediately sent his son to the capital.

sentences.zh: 武興氐姜謨等千餘人上書乞延更限。

translations.literal: More than a thousand of the Wuxing Di led by Jiang Mo submitted a memorial begging to extend Xuan's term.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mo and more than a thousand Wuxing Di submitted a petition asking that Xuan's term be extended.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong approved.

sentences.zh: 宣家世以儒學為業，常慕廉退。

translations.literal: Xuan's family for generations took Confucian learning as their occupation; he always admired integrity and retirement from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's family had pursued Confucian scholarship for generations, and he himself always admired integrity and the willingness to withdraw from office.

sentences.zh: 每歎曰：「以賈誼之才，仕漢文之世，不歷公卿，將非運也！」

translations.literal: He often sighed and said: "With Jia Yi's talents, serving in the age of Emperor Wen of Han, not passing through the ranks of the highest ministers—is it not fate!"
translations.idiomatic: He often sighed, "With talents like Jia Yi's, serving under Emperor Wen of Han yet never reaching the highest offices—is this not the work of fate!

sentences.zh: 乃謂親賓曰：「吾本閭閻之士，素無當世之志，直隨牒推移，遂至於此。

translations.literal: He then said to relatives and guests: "I was originally a man of the lanes and wards, by nature without ambition for the age; I simply followed whatever appointment came and drifted to this point.
translations.idiomatic: He said to relatives and friends, "I was originally a common man of the lanes and wards, with no worldly ambition; I simply accepted whatever appointment came my way and drifted to where I am today.

sentences.zh: 祿後養親，道不光國，瞻言往哲，可以言歸矣。」

translations.literal: With salary I have nourished my parents late in life; my Way has not illumined the state; gazing at the words of sages past, I may speak of returning home."
translations.idiomatic: I have used my salary to support my parents in their old age, yet my service has brought no glory to the state; looking to the example of the sages of old, I believe it is time to speak of retiring.

sentences.zh: 因表求解。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial requesting release from office.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly submitted a memorial requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 世宗不許，乃作懷田賦以敍心焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong did not permit it; he then composed the "Rhapsody on Longing for the Fields" to express his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong refused his request; Xuan then composed "Rhapsody on Longing for the Fields" to express his sentiments.

sentences.zh: 永平四年，患篤，世宗遣太醫令馳驛就視，并賜御藥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongping, seriously ill; Emperor Shizong sent the Director of the Imperial Physicians by post-haste relay to attend him and also bestowed imperial medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Yongping era he fell gravely ill; Emperor Shizong dispatched the Director of the Imperial Physicians by express relay to attend him and bestowed imperial medicines.

sentences.zh: 宣素明陰陽之書，自始患，便知不起，因自剋亡日，果如其言。

translations.literal: Xuan from of old was versed in books of yin and yang; from the onset of illness he knew he would not recover; he therefore himself determined the day of death, and it proved as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had long been versed in the yin-yang arts; from the moment illness set in he knew he would not recover, and he predicted the day of his death—it came to pass exactly as he foretold.

sentences.zh: 時年五十八。

translations.literal: He was fifty-eight at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 世宗悼惜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong mourned and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong grieved his loss.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、豫州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as General of the Left and Governor of Yu province; posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of the Left and Governor of Yu province, with the posthumous title Ding.

sentences.zh: 尋改為穆。

translations.literal: Soon changed to Mu.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous title was soon changed to Mu.

sentences.zh: 子敬憲、莊伯，並在文苑傳。

translations.literal: His sons Jingxian and Zhuangbo are both in the Literary Garden treatise.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jingxian and Zhuangbo both have entries in the Literary Garden treatise.

sentences.zh: 第四子獻伯，武定末，廷尉卿。

translations.literal: The fourth son Xianbo, at the end of the Wuding era, was Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth son Xianbo served as Minister of Justice at the end of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 駿從弟安祖，少而聰慧。

translations.literal: Jun's younger cousin Anzu from early youth was clever and intelligent.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's younger cousin Anzu was clever and quick-witted from childhood.

sentences.zh: 年八九歲，就師講詩，至鹿鳴篇，語諸兄云：「鹿雖禽獸，得食相呼，而況人也？」

translations.literal: At eight or nine years of age, attending his teacher's lectures on the Book of Songs, when he reached the "Deer Cry" ode, he told his elder brothers: "Deer, though beasts, call to one another when they find food—how much more so for men?"
translations.idiomatic: At eight or nine he was studying the Book of Songs with his teacher; when they came to the "Deer Cry," he said to his elder brothers, "Even deer, though they are animals, call to one another when they find food—how much more ought people to do so?"

sentences.zh: 自此之後，未曾獨食。

translations.literal: From then on, he never ate alone.
translations.idiomatic: From that day forward he never ate alone.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: At twenty, the province summoned him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty the province summoned him to serve as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 民有兄弟爭財，詣州相訟。

translations.literal: Some commoners, brothers disputing property, came to the province to sue one another.
translations.idiomatic: When brothers among the people quarreled over property and brought their dispute to the provincial court.

sentences.zh: 安祖召其兄弟，以禮義責讓之。

translations.literal: Anzu summoned the brothers and rebuked them with ritual propriety and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu summoned them and admonished them with appeals to ritual propriety and right conduct.

sentences.zh: 此人兄弟，明日相率謝罪。

translations.literal: These brothers the next day together led one another to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the brothers came together to apologize.

sentences.zh: 內外欽服之。

translations.literal: Within and without all admired and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: People inside and outside the province came to respect him.

sentences.zh: 復有人勸其入仕，安祖曰：「高尚之事，非敢庶幾。

translations.literal: Again someone urged him to enter office; Anzu said: "Lofty and retired conduct—I dare not aspire to it.
translations.idiomatic: When others urged him to take office, Anzu said, "I dare not pretend to lofty reclusion,

sentences.zh: 且京師遼遠，實憚於栖屑耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover the capital is remote and far; I truly dread the vexations of a transient lodging."
translations.idiomatic: and besides, the capital is far away—I truly dread the petty troubles of making a living there."

sentences.zh: 於是閑居養志，不出城邑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lived in retirement cultivating his will, never leaving his town.
translations.idiomatic: So he lived quietly at home nurturing his aspirations and never left his native district.

sentences.zh: 安祖曾行值天熱，舍於樹下。

translations.literal: Anzu once was traveling when it turned hot; he stopped to rest beneath a tree.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while traveling on a hot day, Anzu stopped to rest under a tree.

sentences.zh: 鷙鳥逐雉，雉急投之，遂觸樹而死。

translations.literal: A fierce bird chased a pheasant; the pheasant in panic fled toward him and struck the tree and died.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce bird was chasing a pheasant; the pheasant, in panic, dashed toward him and struck the tree, falling dead.

sentences.zh: 安祖愍之，乃取置陰地，徐徐護視，良久得蘇。

translations.literal: Anzu took pity; he then picked it up and placed it in shade, gently tending and watching it; after long time it revived.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu took pity on it, lifted it into the shade, and gently nursed it until, after a long while, it revived.

sentences.zh: 安祖喜而放之。

translations.literal: Anzu was pleased and released it.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Anzu set it free.

sentences.zh: 後夜忽夢一丈夫，衣冠甚偉，著繡衣曲領，向安祖再拜。

translations.literal: Later one night he suddenly dreamed of a man, his cap and robes very imposing, wearing embroidered garments with a curved collar, who bowed twice to Anzu.
translations.idiomatic: That night he dreamed of a grandly dressed man in embroidered robes with a curved collar, who bowed to him twice.

sentences.zh: 安祖怪而問之。

translations.literal: Anzu marveled and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Astonished, Anzu asked who he was.

sentences.zh: 此人云：「感君前日見放，故來謝德。」

translations.literal: This man said: "Moved by your having released me the other day, I have come to thank your virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "I was moved by your kindness in releasing me the other day and have come to thank you."

sentences.zh: 聞者異焉。

translations.literal: Those who heard of it were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard the story were amazed.

sentences.zh: 後高祖幸長安，至河東，存訪故老。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Gaozu visited Chang'an; reaching Hedong, he made inquiries after old worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Gaozu visited Chang'an and, reaching Hedong, sought out elderly men of worth.

sentences.zh: 安祖朝於蒲坂，高祖與語甚悅，仍拜安邑令。

translations.literal: Anzu presented himself at Puban; Emperor Gaozu spoke with him and was very pleased, and straightaway appointed him Magistrate of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu came to Puban to pay his respects; the emperor took great pleasure in conversation with him and immediately appointed him magistrate of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 安祖以老病固辭，詔給一時俸，以供湯藥焉。

translations.literal: Anzu on grounds of age and illness firmly declined; an edict granted a temporary salary to supply medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu firmly declined on account of age and illness; the court granted him a temporary stipend for medicines.

sentences.zh: 年八十三，卒於家。

translations.literal: At age eighty-three, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 子思濟，亦有志操，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Siji also had will and integrity, but died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Siji was likewise a man of integrity and aspiration, but died young.

sentences.zh: 子宗賢。

translations.literal: His son Zongxian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zongxian.

sentences.zh: 思濟弟幼儁，卒於猗氏令。

translations.literal: Siji's younger brother Youjun died while serving as Magistrate of Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: Siji's younger brother Youjun died while serving as magistrate of Yishi.

sentences.zh: 辛紹先，隴西狄道人。

translations.literal: Xin Shaoxian was a native of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Shaoxian was from Didao in Longxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 五世祖怡，晉幽州刺史。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Yi was Jin Governor of You province.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Yi had served as governor of You province under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父淵，私署涼王李暠驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was Swift Cavalry General under the self-appointed King of Liang Li Gao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan served as Swift Cavalry General under Li Gao, the self-declared King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 暠子歆亦厚遇之。

translations.literal: Gao's son Xin also treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao's son Xin likewise treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 歆與沮渠蒙遜戰於蓼泉，軍敗失馬，淵以所乘馬援歆，而身死於難，以義烈見稱西土。

translations.literal: Xin fought Juqu Mengsun at Liaoquan; the army was defeated and he lost his horse; Yuan gave Xin the horse he was riding and himself died in the crisis—by righteous valor he was praised throughout the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin fought Juqu Mengsun at Liaoquan and his army was defeated, he lost his horse; Yuan gave Xin his own mount and died in the battle, winning renown in the west for his righteous sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 世祖之平涼州，紹先內徙，家於晉陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang province, Shaoxian moved inward and made his home at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang province, Shaoxian was resettled inland and established his household at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 明敏有識量，與廣平游明根、范陽盧度世、同郡李承等甚相友善。

translations.literal: Clear and keen with judgment and capacity, with Guangping's You Minggen, Fanyang's Lu Dushi, and his fellow townsman Li Cheng he was very friendly.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligent and perceptive, he was close friends with You Minggen of Guangping, Lu Dushi of Fanyang, Li Cheng of his home commandery, and others.

sentences.zh: 有至性，丁父憂，三年口不甘味，頭不櫛沐，髮遂落盡，故常著垂裙皂帽。

translations.literal: He had utmost filial nature; observing mourning for his father, for three years his mouth knew no savor, his head received no combing or washing, and his hair then fell out entirely—therefore he always wore a drooping-skirt black cap.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial, during three years of mourning for his father he took no pleasure in food, did not comb or wash his hair until it all fell out, and thereafter always wore a black cap with a drooping skirt of cloth.

sentences.zh: 自中書博士，轉神部令。

translations.literal: From Doctor of the Secretariat he was transferred to Director of the Spiritual Department.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Doctor of the Secretariat to Director of the Spiritual Department.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，薛安都以彭城歸國，時朝廷欲綏安初附，以紹先為下邳太守，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era, Xue Andu returned to the realm from Pengcheng; the court then wished to pacify and reassure the newly submitted; Shaoxian was made Governor of Xiapi and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangxing era, when Xue Andu defected from Pengcheng back to Wei, the court sought to reassure his newly submitted followers and appointed Shaoxian governor of Xiapi with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 為政不苟激察，舉其大綱而已，唯教民治產禦賊之備。

translations.literal: In governing he was not harsh or overly inquisitive; he handled only the broad outlines, teaching the people only to manage property and prepare against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He governed without harsh scrutiny, attending to broad principles alone while instructing the people to manage their livelihoods and prepare defenses against bandits.

sentences.zh: 及劉彧將陳顯達、蕭道成、蕭順之來寇，道成謂順之曰：「辛紹先未易侵也，宜共慎之。」

translations.literal: When Liu Yu's generals Chen Xianda, Xiao Daocheng, and Xiao Shunzhi came to raid, Daocheng said to Shunzhi: "Xin Shaoxian is not easy to invade; we should together be cautious toward him."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu's generals Chen Xianda, Xiao Daocheng, and Xiao Shunzhi launched an attack, Daocheng told Shunzhi, "Xin Shaoxian is not an easy mark—we must be careful together."

sentences.zh: 於是不歷郡境，遂徑屯呂梁。

translations.literal: Thereupon they did not enter the commandery territory, but went straight to encamp at Lüliang.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore bypassed the commandery entirely and encamped directly at Lüliang.

sentences.zh: 太和十三年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 贈冠軍將軍、并州刺史、晉陽公，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Champion General, Governor of Bing province, and Duke of Jinyang; posthumous title Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Champion General, Governor of Bing province, and Duke of Jinyang, with the posthumous title Hui.

sentences.zh: 子鳳達，耽道樂古，有長者之名。

translations.literal: His son Fengda devoted himself to the Way and delighted in antiquity; he had the reputation of an elder of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengda was devoted to learning and antiquity and enjoyed a reputation as a man of mature integrity.

sentences.zh: 卒於京兆王子推國常侍。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Regular Attendant in the domain of Prince of Jingzhao Zituo.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Regular Attendant in the household of Prince of Jingzhao Zituo.

sentences.zh: 鳳達子祥，字萬褔。

translations.literal: Fengda's son Xiang, courtesy name Wanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Fengda's son Xiang, courtesy name Wanfu.

sentences.zh: 舉司州秀才。

translations.literal: Recommended as Provincial Outstanding Talented Candidate of Si province.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as a Provincial Outstanding Talented Candidate from Si province.

sentences.zh: 司空行參軍，遷主簿。

translations.literal: Acting Staff Officer on the staff of the Excellency of Works; transferred to Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Acting Staff Officer on the staff of the Excellency of Works and was promoted to Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 太傅元丕為并州刺史，祥為丕府屬，敕行建興郡。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yuan Pi was Governor of Bing province; Xiang was a staff member of Pi's bureau and was ordered to act as Administrator of Jianxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Tutor Yuan Pi became governor of Bing province, Xiang served on his staff and was ordered to administer Jianxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧妃即祥妻妹，及禧構逆，親知多罹塵謗，祥獨蕭然不預。

translations.literal: Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi's consort was Xiang's wife's younger sister; when Xi plotted rebellion, relatives and acquaintances for the most part suffered calumny; Xiang alone remained detached and uninvolved.
translations.idiomatic: The consort of Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi was Xiang's wife's younger sister; when Xi plotted rebellion, many of Xiang's relatives and acquaintances were tainted by the scandal, but Xiang alone remained unstained and uninvolved.

sentences.zh: 轉并州平北府司馬。

translations.literal: Transferred to Major of the Pacify-the-North headquarters of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Major in the Pacify-the-North headquarters of Bing province.

sentences.zh: 會刺史喪，朝廷以其公清，遂越長史，敕行州事。

translations.literal: It happened that the governor died; the court, because of his fairness and integrity, thereupon skipped over the Senior Clerk and ordered him to administer provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the governor died, the court, trusting his integrity, passed over the Senior Clerk and ordered him to administer the province.

sentences.zh: 祥初在司馬，有白壁還兵藥道顯被誣為賊，官屬推處，咸以為然。

translations.literal: When Xiang was first serving as Major, at Baiyuan in the Returning Armies Yao Daoxian was slandered as a bandit; the office staff investigated and judged the case, and all thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiang was still Major, a soldier of the Returning Armies at Baiyuan named Yao Daoxian was falsely accused of banditry; the office staff investigated and all assumed the charge was true.

sentences.zh: 祥曰：「道顯面有悲色，察獄以色，其此之謂乎？」

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Daoxian's face bears a look of grief—'observe lawsuits by countenance'—is this not what is meant?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Daoxian's face shows grief—when one inspects a case, one reads the countenance—is this not such a case?"

sentences.zh: 苦執申之。

translations.literal: He strenuously insisted on vindicating him.
translations.idiomatic: He argued strenuously on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 月餘，別獲真賊。

translations.literal: After more than a month, the real bandit was captured separately.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later the real culprits were caught elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 後除郢州龍驤府長史，帶義陽太守。

translations.literal: Later appointed Senior Clerk of the Dragon-Prancing headquarters of Ying province, concurrently Governor of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Senior Clerk of the Dragon-Prancing headquarters of Ying province and concurrently served as governor of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 白早生之反也，蕭衍遣眾來援，因此緣淮鎮戍，相繼降沒，唯祥堅城獨守。

translations.literal: When Bai Zaosheng rebelled, Xiao Yan sent troops to aid him; on this account the garrison posts along the Huai successively surrendered and were lost—only Xiang held the city firm and defended alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Zaosheng rebelled, Xiao Yan sent troops to support him; one by one the Huai River garrisons surrendered, but Xiang alone held his city steadfastly.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將胡武城、陶平虜於州南金山之上連營侵逼，眾情大懼。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent the generals Hu Wucheng and Tao Pinglu; on Golden Mountain south of the province they connected camps and pressed the attack; the people's sentiment was greatly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent generals Hu Wucheng and Tao Pinglu, who linked camps on Golden Mountain south of the province and pressed the siege; morale collapsed in fear.

sentences.zh: 祥從容曉喻，人心遂安。

translations.literal: Xiang calmly explained and instructed; people's hearts then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang calmly reassured the garrison, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 時出挑戰，偽退以驕賊。

translations.literal: At times he went out to challenge battle, feigning retreat to make the bandits arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: He occasionally sallied forth to challenge the enemy, feigning retreat to lull them into overconfidence.

sentences.zh: 賊果日來攻逼，不復自備，乃夜出襲其營。

translations.literal: The bandits truly came day after day to attack and press; no longer guarding themselves, he then by night went out and raided their camp.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, emboldened, attacked daily without maintaining proper defenses; Xiang then led a night raid on their camp.

sentences.zh: 將曉，矢刃交下，賊大崩散潰，擒平虜，斬武城，以送京師，州境獲全。

translations.literal: Near dawn, arrows and blades rained down; the bandits greatly collapsed, scattered, and routed; Pinglu was captured, Wucheng beheaded, and both sent to the capital; the provincial territory was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, as arrows and blades flew, the enemy army collapsed in rout; Xiang captured Tao Pinglu, beheaded Hu Wucheng, sent both to the capital, and preserved the province intact.

sentences.zh: 論功方有賞授，而刺史婁悅耻勳出其下，聞之執政，事竟不行。

translations.literal: When merits were being discussed for reward and appointment, Governor Lou Yue was ashamed that the achievement ranked below him; he reported it to those in power; the matter in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were being considered, Governor Lou Yue, shamed that the credit should go to a subordinate, complained to the central authorities, and in the end no reward was granted.

sentences.zh: 胡賊劉龍駒作逆華州，敕除祥華州永安王爕征虜府長史，仍為別將，與討胡使薛和討滅之。

translations.literal: The Hu bandit Liu Longju rebelled in Hua province; by edict Xiang was appointed Senior Clerk on the Conquer-the-Barbarians staff of Prince of Yong'an Yuan Ye of Hua province, and also served as a separate commander; together with the Bandit-Suppression Commissioner Xue He he attacked and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hu rebel Liu Longju rose in Hua province, Xiang was appointed Senior Clerk on the Conquer-the-Barbarians staff of Prince of Yong'an Yuan Ye and also served as a separate commander; with Bandit-Suppression Commissioner Xue He he destroyed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年卒，時年五十五。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengui he died; he was then fifty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Shengui at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，贈冠軍將軍、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an, posthumously honored as Champion General and Governor of Southern Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongan he was posthumously honored as Champion General and Governor of Southern Qing province.

sentences.zh: 長子琨，字懷玉，少聰敏。

translations.literal: The eldest son Kun, courtesy name Huaiyu, was clever and keen from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Kun, courtesy name Huaiyu, was bright and quick-witted from childhood.

sentences.zh: 解褐相州倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office he was Army Master of Storage of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: On entering service he was appointed Army Master of Storage in Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 稍遷陳郡太守、輕車將軍、濟州征虜府長史。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted to Governor of Chen commandery, General of the Light Chariots, and Senior Clerk of the Conquer-the-Barbarians headquarters of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to governor of Chen commandery, General of the Light Chariots, and Senior Clerk of the Conquer-the-Barbarians headquarters of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: He died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 琨弟懷仁，武定末，長樂太守。

translations.literal: Kun's younger brother Huairen, at the end of the Wuding era, was Governor of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Kun's younger brother Huairen served as governor of Changle at the end of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 懷仁弟賁，字叔文。

translations.literal: Huairen's younger brother Ben, courtesy name Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Huairen's younger brother Ben, courtesy name Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 少有文學，識度沉雅。

translations.literal: From youth he had literary learning; his judgment and bearing were serene and refined.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was accomplished in letters, and his judgment and bearing were calm and refined.

sentences.zh: 起家北中府中兵參軍、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Upon beginning his career he was Central Troops Staff Officer of the Northern Center headquarters and Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Central Troops Staff Officer of the Northern Center headquarters and Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 建義初，修起居注。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he compiled the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era he served as compiler of the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 除濟州撫軍府長史。

translations.literal: Appointed Senior Clerk of the Pacify-the-Army headquarters of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Senior Clerk of the Pacify-the-Army headquarters of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，轉膠州車騎府長史，遷平東將軍，太師、咸陽王坦開府長史。

translations.literal: In Emperor Chu's time, transferred to Senior Clerk of the Chariots-and-Cavalry headquarters of Jiao province; promoted to General Who Pacifies the East; Senior Clerk on the staff of the Grand Preceptor, Prince of Xianyang Yuan Tan's open headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chu he became Senior Clerk of the Chariots-and-Cavalry headquarters of Jiao province, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East, and served as Senior Clerk on the staff of Grand Preceptor Yuan Tan, Prince of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 武定中，中尉崔暹表薦賁，除

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, Censor-in-Chief Cui Xian memorialized recommending Ben; appointed
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era, Censor-in-Chief Cui Xian recommended Ben, who was appointed

translations.literal: 〈Lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Lacuna〉

sentences.zh: 太守。

translations.literal: Governor.
translations.idiomatic: governor.

sentences.zh: 吏民懷其恩惠。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners cherished his gracious kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and people cherished his kindness.

sentences.zh: 還，卒於鄴。

translations.literal: On his return, he died at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he died at Ye.

sentences.zh: 時年五十八。

translations.literal: He was then fifty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 賁弟烈，字季武。

translations.literal: Ben's younger brother Lie, courtesy name Jiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Ben's younger brother Lie, courtesy name Jiwu.

sentences.zh: 歷太傅東閤祭酒，卒於梁州鎮南府長史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Grand Tutor; he died while Senior Clerk of the Pacify-the-South headquarters of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion on the staff of the Grand Tutor and died while Senior Clerk of the Pacify-the-South headquarters in Liang province.

sentences.zh: 烈弟匡，字季政，頗有文學。

translations.literal: Lie's younger brother Kuang, courtesy name Jizheng, had considerable literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's younger brother Kuang, courtesy name Jizheng, was fairly accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 永安初，釋褐封丘令，加威烈將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongan, upon first taking office he became Magistrate of Fengqiu and was given the additional title General of Majestic Valor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongan era he entered service as magistrate of Fengqiu with the additional rank of General of Majestic Valor.

sentences.zh: 時經河陰之役，朝士多求出外，故匡為之。

translations.literal: At the time, having passed through the Battle of Heyin, court gentlemen mostly sought to go out to the provinces; therefore Kuang took such a post.
translations.idiomatic: After the Battle of Heyin, many court officials sought provincial posts, and Kuang took one for that reason.

sentences.zh: 後除平遠將軍、符璽郎中。

translations.literal: Later appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Gentleman of Seals and Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Gentleman of Seals and Credentials.

sentences.zh: 卒於龍驤將軍、通直散騎侍郎，時年三十五。

translations.literal: He died while holding the posts of Dragon-Prancing General and Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; he was then thirty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Dragon-Prancing General and Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary at the age of thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、前將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Forward General, and Governor of Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Forward General, and Governor of Yong province.

sentences.zh: 祥弟少雍，字季仲。

translations.literal: Xiang's younger brother Shaoyong, courtesy name Jizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's younger brother Shaoyong, courtesy name Jizhong.

sentences.zh: 少聰穎，有孝行，尤為祖父紹先所愛。

translations.literal: From youth clever and quick; he had filial conduct; especially by his grandfather Shaoxian he was loved.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood and filial, he was especially beloved by his grandfather Shaoxian.

sentences.zh: 紹先性嗜羊肝，常呼少雍共食。

translations.literal: Shaoxian by nature loved sheep's liver; he often summoned Shaoyong to eat together.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxian had a fondness for sheep's liver and often called Shaoyong to share it with him.

sentences.zh: 及紹先卒，少雍終身不食肝。

translations.literal: When Shaoxian died, Shaoyong for his whole life did not eat liver.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaoxian died, Shaoyong never ate liver for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 性仁厚，有禮義，門內之法，為時所重。

translations.literal: His nature was benevolent and generous; he had ritual propriety and righteousness; the rules within his household were by the age held in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolent and courteous, he upheld household standards that contemporaries greatly respected.

sentences.zh: 釋褐奉朝請，太學博士、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office: Attendant-in-Ordinary in Regular Attendance; Imperial University Erudite; Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: On entering service he was Attendant-in-Ordinary in Regular Attendance, Imperial University Erudite, and Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 司空、高陽王雍引為田曹參軍。

translations.literal: The Excellency of Works, Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong, recruited him as Field Bureau Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong, in his capacity as Excellency of Works, recruited him as Field Bureau Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 少雍性清正，不憚強禦，積年久訟，造次決之，請託路絕，時稱賢明。

translations.literal: Shaoyong's nature was pure and upright; he did not fear the powerful; lawsuits piled up over many years—he decided them on the spot; the path of influence-seeking was cut off; the age called him worthy and clear-sighted.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyong was upright and fearless before the powerful; he disposed on the spot of lawsuits that had dragged on for years, shut down the avenue of private influence, and was acclaimed at the time as a wise administrator.

sentences.zh: 正始中，詔百官各舉所知，高陽王雍及吏部郎中李憲俱以少雍為舉首。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era, an edict ordered every official to recommend men he knew; Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong and Bureau Director Li Xian of the Ministry of Personnel both put Shaoyong at the head of their lists.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era, an edict ordered all officials to recommend men they knew; Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong and Li Xian, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel, both ranked Shaoyong first.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 侍中游肇後亦薦之，會卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary You Zhao also recommended him later; he happened to die, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary You Zhao also recommended him afterward, but Shaoyong happened to die, aged forty-two.

sentences.zh: 少雍妻王氏，有德義，與其從子懷仁兄弟同居，懷仁等事之甚謹，閨門禮讓，人無比焉。

translations.literal: Shaoyong's wife, née Wang, had virtue and righteousness; with her husband's cousins Huairen and his brothers she lived together; Huairen and the others served her with great deference; within the household courtesy and yielding prevailed as in no other family.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyong's wife, née Wang, was virtuous and upright; she lived together with her husband's cousins Huairen and his brothers, and they served her with scrupulous deference. Courtesy and forbearance within the household were unmatched.

sentences.zh: 士大夫以此稱美。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials on this account praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials praised them for it.

sentences.zh: 子元植，武定中，儀同府司馬。

translations.literal: His son Yuanzhi, in the Wuding era, served as staff commander on an Equaling-the-Three-Ministers headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanzhi served during the Wuding era as staff commander on an Equaling-the-Three-Ministers headquarters.

sentences.zh: 元植弟士遜，太師開府功曹參軍。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi's younger brother Shixun served as Merit Officer on the Grand Preceptor's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi's younger brother Shixun served as Merit Officer on the Grand Preceptor's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 鳳達弟穆，字叔宗。

translations.literal: Feng Da's younger brother Mu, courtesy name Shuzong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Da's younger brother Mu, courtesy name Shuzong.

sentences.zh: 舉茂才，東雍州別駕。

translations.literal: Recommended as Outstanding Talent; Vice-Prefect of Eastern Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Outstanding Talent, he served as Vice-Prefect of Eastern Yong province.

sentences.zh: 初隨父在下邳，與彭城陳敬文友善。

translations.literal: At first he followed his father to Xiapi and became friends with Chen Jingwen of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At first he followed his father to Xiapi, where he became friends with Chen Jingwen of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 敬文弟敬武，少為沙門，從師遠學，經久不反。

translations.literal: Jingwen's younger brother Jingwu, as a youth became a Buddhist monk and went far away to study with a teacher; for a long time he did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen's younger brother Jingwu had become a Buddhist monk in youth and gone far away to study; he did not return for many years.

sentences.zh: 敬文病臨卒，以雜綾二十匹，託穆與敬武。

translations.literal: Jingwen fell ill and was near death; he entrusted twenty bolts of mixed silk to Mu for delivery to Jingwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingwen fell mortally ill, he entrusted twenty bolts of mixed silk to Mu for delivery to Jingwu.

sentences.zh: 穆久訪不得。

translations.literal: Mu searched for a long time without finding him.
translations.idiomatic: Mu searched for a long time without finding him.

sentences.zh: 經二十餘年，始於洛陽見敬武，以物還之，封題如故，世稱其廉信。

translations.literal: After more than twenty years he finally met Jingwu in Luoyang, returned the goods to him with the seals and inscriptions intact; the age called his integrity and trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty years he finally met Jingwu in Luoyang and returned the goods with the seals and inscriptions intact; contemporaries praised his integrity and trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 歷東荊州司馬，轉長史，帶義陽太守，領戍。

translations.literal: He served as Administrator of Eastern Jing province, was transferred to chief clerk, concurrently governor of Yiyang, and overseer of the frontier garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Eastern Jing province, then became chief clerk, concurrently governor of Yiyang and overseer of the frontier garrison.

sentences.zh: 雅有恤民之稱。

translations.literal: He had a reputation for compassion toward the people.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a reputation for compassion toward the people.

sentences.zh: 轉汝陽太守，值水澇民飢，上表請輕租賦。

translations.literal: Transferred to governor of Ruyang; when floodwaters inundated the land and the people suffered famine, he memorialized the throne requesting lighter land tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to governor of Ruyang, he found the land flooded and the people starving; he memorialized the throne requesting lighter taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，遂敕汝陽一郡，聽以小絹為調。

translations.literal: The emperor approved, and so ordered the whole commandery of Ruyang to be allowed to pay tribute in fine silk instead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered the entire commandery of Ruyang to pay tribute in fine silk instead.

sentences.zh: 遷中散大夫，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Promoted to Grand Master of Palace Leisure and given the additional title General of the Flying Dragons.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Leisure and given the additional title General of the Flying Dragons.

sentences.zh: 正光四年，以老啟求致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengguang, on account of age he petitioned requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengguang he petitioned on account of age to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 詔引見，謂穆志力尚可，除平原相。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him for an audience; the emperor said Mu's will and strength were still adequate and appointed him governor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him for an audience; the emperor said Mu's will and strength were still adequate and appointed him governor of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 穆善撫導，民吏懷之。

translations.literal: Mu was skilled at comforting and guiding; officials and commoners all cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was skilled at comforting and guiding the people, and officials and commoners alike cherished him.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年，徵為征虜將軍、太中大夫，未發，卒於郡，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaochang he was summoned as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Counsel; before he set out he died in the commandery, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaochang he was summoned as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, but before he set out he died in the commandery, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈後將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Rear General and Inspector of You province; posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Rear General and Inspector of You province, with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 長子子馥，字元穎，早有學行。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zifu, courtesy name Yuanying, from early showed learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zifu, courtesy name Yuanying, showed learning and upright conduct from an early age.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，釋褐南司州龍驤府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he entered office as Recording Officer on the Dragon Might headquarters of Southern Si province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaochang he entered office as Recording Officer on the Dragon Might headquarters of Southern Si province.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，居喪有禮。

translations.literal: Upon entering mourning for his father, his observance of the rites was correct.
